items.summary: The larger the Lefschetz defect delta(X) of a smooth complex Fano variety X, the more information we can deduce about the geometry of X. The structure of varieties with delta(X) greater than 2 is known. In this paper, we study the case delta(X)=2. In particular, we focus on Fano varieties with delta(X)=2 arising from the so called Casagrande-Druel construction, which we refer to as Construction A. We show that among the 19 families of Fano 3-folds with delta(X)=2 classified by Mori and Mukai, 15 arise from such construction. Moreover, we construct all Fano 4-folds with Picard number greater than 3 and delta(X)=2 admitting such a structure, obtaining 145 distinct families in total. This completes the classification of all Casagrande-Druel Fano 4-folds with delta(X)=2. To broaden the scope, we also study a generalized version of Construction A, which we call Construction B, and we show that 18 out of the 19 families of Fano 3-folds with delta(X)=2 arise from it.

items.title: Brown Measures and Spectral Convergence for Arbitrary GUE Polynomials
items.summary: We prove that, for every noncommutative polynomial in independent GUE matrices, the empirical eigenvalue distribution converges almost surely to the Brown measure of the same polynomial in free semicircular variables. This is the Gaussian case of a conjecture of Belinschi, Śniady and Speicher. We also prove that the spectrum converges almost surely in Hausdorff distance to the spectrum of the limiting operator, so that the spectral radius converges as well; deviations have probability smaller than every inverse power of the matrix size. For this we show that the support of the Brown measure of every polynomial in free semicircular variables is its whole spectrum, a statement about operators that involves no random matrices. We also give an algorithm, with a convergence guarantee, that computes the limiting Brown measure from matrices whose size depends only on the polynomial. A holomorphic rotation introduces an independent Ginibre component and yields the almost-sure limit without a least-singular-value bound for the original GUE polynomial. We also give a second-moment criterion for weak convergence of Brown measures. On free probability side, we use the Dyson equation of a linear pencil to show that harmonicity of its logarithmic potential forces invertibility.

items.title: Stable finiteness and combination theorems for Hughes-free embeddings
items.summary: We show that all group algebras of Higman's group and Deligne's group are stably finite. We also study when the Hughes-free embeddability property is closed under taking graphs of groups, and give a positive answer when the edge maps are retractions or injective on Abelianisations. As a consequence we obtain that fundamental groups of graphs of torsion-free Abelian groups, graph products of locally indicable Hughes-free embeddable groups, and fundamental groups of graphs of free groups with cyclic edge groups are Hughes-free embeddable.

items.title: Cohomology of pseudo-reductive groups over local function fields
items.summary: We give a pairing which describes the first Galois cohomology of a pseudo-reductive group $G$ over a local function field $K$ as the Pontryagin dual of the group $\Ext^1(G, \Gm)$ of translation-invariant line bundles on $G$. In order to accomplish this, we endow the Picard group of a scheme $X$ over a (Hausdorff) topological field with a topology, and prove that this topology enjoys favorable properties under certain mild conditions on $X$ and on the field.

items.title: Large deviations for integrated exponentials of Gaussian Volterra processes - application to variance options
items.summary: We prove small-time large deviations for the normalised time integral of the exponential of a Gaussian Volterra process, and complement it with a central limit theorem and moderate deviations. As an application, we obtain short-maturity asymptotics for out-of-the-money and at-the-money variance options in rough volatility models, as well as implied volatility expansions which we validate numerically.

items.title: Pietsch's favourite problem on singular traces
items.summary: In 2023, A. Pietsch formulated twenty-seven open problems concerning traces on operator ideals. We give an affirmative answer to Problem 16, which Pietsch singled out as his personal favourite, by constructing a nonzero bounded singular spectral trace on the weak Weyl ideal over the class of all Banach spaces.

items.title: Bolognesi's Conjecture for Nonnegative-Charge Iterated Magnetic Bags
items.summary: We establish a magnetic-bag limit for smooth $SU(2)$ Bogomolny monopoles associated with finitely many nested smooth surfaces in $\mathbb{R}^3$. This proves Bolognesi's magnetic-bag conjecture for iterated magnetic bags with nonnegative charge density on each surface.

items.title: A second-order relaxation system for a degenerate-parabolic quasilinear fourth-order rimming-flow equation with critical spectrum
items.summary: For a spectrally critical nonlinear degenerate-parabolic PDE of fourth-order, describing a capillary-driven fluid flow in a rotating cylinder, we propose a second-order relaxation system of parabolic-elliptic type. For positive initial data, we prove local existence and uniqueness of solutions to the relaxation system. Thereby, the lifespan of the approximate solutions turns out to be independent of the relaxation parameter. Moreover, we prove convergence of non-negative weak solutions of the relaxation system to weak solutions of the original equation on compact time intervals. We classify positive steady states of the relaxed system, prove a stability result yielding global strong solutions, and show that the long-time dynamics remain consistent under the relaxation limit.

items.title: Conics and rational points of bounded height on cubic surfaces
items.summary: We construct auxiliary intersections covering points of bounded height on geometrically integral non-ruled cubic surfaces over a fixed number field, and prove uniform bounds for the contribution of their conic components to rational and integral point counts. In the affine case, when the section at infinity is geometrically integral, the conic contribution admits a bound with a height exponent strictly below one. Under these hypotheses and within the same covering, obtaining a uniform bound for all integral points with any exponent greater than one reduces to controlling components of degree at least three. The proof combines a form of the global determinant method that retains the dependence on the height of Cayley form with uniform estimates for the number of conics of bounded height. The Deligne pairing and the geometry of residual conic pencils yield cubic image curves in fixed coefficient spaces. Uniform point estimates on these curves control the distribution of conic heights, with constants independent of the surface and the pencil.

items.title: Simple zeros of the Riemann zeta-function: a local multiplicity test and long mixed moments
items.summary: Assuming the Riemann Hypothesis, we show that at least 71.274066\% of the nontrivial zeros of $ζ(s)$ are simple, and at least 85.368230% are distinct. The previous bounds were 19/27 $\approx$ 70.37%, due to Conrey, Ghosh and Gonek and to Bui and Heath-Brown (2013), and 84.77\%, due to Chirre, Gonçalves and de Laat (2020). The method combines the two classical approaches to simple zeros. Montgomery's pair correlation argument rests on a pointwise consequence of the explicit formula: at a zero of multiplicity $m\ge2$, a Dirichlet polynomial $J$ over prime powers of length $T^ψ$, $ψ<1$, is forced to have real part at most $-a<0$. The mollified derivative $ζ'(ρ)M(ρ)$ of Conrey, Ghosh and Gonek vanishes there. Both facts are used at the same zero, in a single least-squares inequality. The new analytic input is the mixed moment $\sum_ρζ'(ρ)M(ρ)J(1-ρ)$ with $J$ much longer than the mollifier. We evaluate it under the Riemann Hypothesis alone; the long prime sum stays in the numerator and the mollifier variable is the modulus, so the barrier at $T^{1/2}$ does not arise. A second-order version of the argument gives $0.70736$. We show that no second-order certificate of this type can exceed $0.7073646063$, and pass this ceiling with fourth moments of short Dirichlet polynomials and with mixed moments against products of a bounded number of primes. All constants are certified in exact rational arithmetic.

items.title: Quantitative BMO-BLO Estimates for the Hardy-Littlewood Maximal Function
items.summary: In this note, we study a quantitative extension of the John-Nirenberg inequality for the Hardy-Littlewood maximal function of a $\operatorname{BMO}$ function. More precisely, for every nonconstant locally integrable function $f$ such that $Mf$ is not identically infinite, we prove the inequality \begin{equation*} \left( \frac{1}{w(Q)}\int_Q \left( \frac{Mf(x) - \operatorname{ess\,inf}_{Q} Mf }{M^\# f(x)} \right)^p w(x)\,dx\right)^\frac{1}{p} \le c_n \, [w]_{A_\infty}\, p \end{equation*} for every cube $Q$, every $1\le p<\infty$ and every weight $w\in A_\infty$, where $[w]_{A_\infty}$ denotes the Fujii-Wilson $A_\infty$ constant. This result extends the classical boundedness $\|Mf\|_{\operatorname{BLO}}\le C_n\|f\|_{\operatorname{BMO}}$ proved by Bennett, DeVore, and Sharpley (Ann. of Math. (2) 113 (1981)) and by Bennett (Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. 85 (1982)). Furthermore, we show that the class $A_\infty$ is both necessary and sufficient for this inequality to hold, providing a new characterization of $A_\infty$ in terms of the action of the maximal operator on bounded oscillation spaces.

items.title: Gravitational collapse to extremal black holes with $Λ>0$: counterexamples to the third law without charge
items.summary: We study the dynamical formation of the extremal Schwarzschild-de Sitter solution, in both its time orientations, and the related Nariai solution. We prove that there exist spherically symmetric, regular Cauchy data for the Einstein-scalar field system with $\mathbb S^3$ topology, for any scalar field mass $\mathfrak{m}\geq 0$, that lead to the formation of an exactly extremal Schwarzschild-de Sitter black hole in finite time, and that moreover the apparent horizon of the solution is exactly isometric to that of the subextremal Schwarzschild-de Sitter solution at earlier times. We also show that if the scalar field mass satisfies $\mathfrak{m}>\sqrtΛ/2$, an analogous result holds having the extremal Schwarzschild-de Sitter white hole or the Nariai solution in place of the black hole. In the black hole case, the exactly extremal Schwarzschild-de Sitter region is bounded to the future by two event horizons and can be seen as the analogue of the exterior region in the asymptotically flat case. We moreover establish that these two black hole horizons that bound the exactly extremal Schwarzschild-de Sitter region are the only event horizons present in the spacetime, something non-trivial given the existence of multi-black hole configurations when $Λ> 0$. Consequently, the solutions arising from these data can be thought to constitute, in particular, regular counterexamples to the third law of black hole thermodynamics with $Λ>0$ arising from the collapse of physically plausible matter which is moreover uncharged. Our approach to construct the Cauchy data relies on $C^k$ characteristic gluing results for the Einstein-scalar field system in spherical symmetry, in the spirit of [KU25].

items.title: Hall's condition between adjacent levels of the face lattice of the permutohedron
items.summary: Let $\OP$ be the poset of ordered set partitions of $[n]$, ordered by merging adjacent blocks; with a bottom element adjoined it is the face lattice of the permutohedron. Whether it has the Sperner property is open. We show that for every pair of adjacent levels, the smaller one can be matched into the larger one by parent--child pairs, except possibly for the pairs $(j,j+1)$ with $(28n-36)/39<j<(13n+5)/18$ (for small $n$ the window is slightly smaller still). This window has width about $n/234\approx0.0043\,n$. The largest level lies near $n/(2\ln2)\approx0.7213\,n$, which we prove using the law of the block sizes of a uniformly random ordered set partition of $[n]$, and for $n$ large it falls inside the window. Since the level sizes are log-concave, Hall's condition for all pairs would make $\OP$ Sperner. The proofs use explicit weights on the parent--child pairs; they reduce to a finite inequality between pairs of adjacent blocks. We explain why the simplest weights fail exactly at the boundary of a much larger window, and report computations supporting Hall's condition inside the window: exactly for $n\le14$, and by equalizing flows for every window pair with $n\le25$.

items.title: Square-root comparison, Turnpike, and exact semidefinite feasibility
items.summary: Given positive integers $a_i,K$, put $S=\sum_{i=1}^k\sqrt{a_i}$. We construct a realizable Turnpike instance in which the minimum spacing of distinct distances and the smallest nonzero addition residual are both at most $|S-K|$ when $S\ne K$. With approximation oracles, one three-distance realizability query decides $S\le K$. For unordered lists of radical sums with nonnegative rational coefficients, a polynomial-time substitution by integers preserves every normalized ruler. We give the classical reduction of square-root comparison to exact semidefinite feasibility in both threshold directions. The comparison enters through numerical separation and marked sorting; the integer recoding needs no such comparison for unordered reconstruction.

items.title: Viscosity solutions for integro-differential equations with gradient and source terms
items.summary: We address global well-posedness for integro-differential equations with gradient and source terms. This naturally results from establishing the comparison principle for viscosity solutions and existence via Perron's method. There are many earlier results for similar equations, and our work attempts to give a unified approach and improve upon some recent examples. There is a natural juxtaposition of earlier results in the usual framework of viscosity solutions which rely on a min-max structure, with some more recent implementations coming from the free boundary literature in which a min-max is not apparent initially, but does appear a posteriori due to certain rigid structural constraints. Here we give a presentation that combines ideas from both situations. The most important feature of the operators in our equations is what we call the global comparison property. This is combined with a natural local Lipschitz assumption on the operator defining the equation.

items.title: Convergence of Residual-driven Adaptive Kernel-based Multilevel Approximation
items.summary: Kernel-based multilevel methods combine compactly supported radial basis functions with a residual correction scheme and are known to converge linearly in the number of levels. In this paper we study an adaptive version of the multilevel method, in which the interpolation on each level only uses those sites at which the residual of the preceding level exceeds a given threshold. Although this method has been proposed some time ago and converges in all numerical tests, a convergence proof has been missing so far. We close this gap. We derive an a priori error bound, an a posteriori error bound valid for arbitrary point selections, and extend the analysis to penalized least-squares approximation and to target functions outside the native space of the kernel. For a variant with an additional check-loop per level, we show convergence with the rate of the classical multilevel method. We illustrate our findings with three numerical examples.

items.title: On infinite torsion of abelian varieties over large algebraic fields of positive characteristic
items.summary: Let $A$ be a non-zero abelian variety defined over a finitely generated field $F$. A conjecture of Geyer and Jarden [GJ78] asserts that for every $σ\in \mathrm{Gal}(F^{sep}/F)$ outside a set of Haar measure zero, there exist infinitely many primes $\ell$ such that the $\ell$-torsion subgroup of $A(F^{sep}(σ))$ is non-zero (or equivalently, the torsion subgroup of $A(F^{sep}(σ))$ is infinite), where $F^{sep}(σ)$ denotes the subfield of $F^{sep}$ fixed by $σ$. While this conjecture remains open when $\mathrm{Char}(F)>0$, we establish a new case under the assumptions of $\mathrm{End}(A)=\mathbb{Z}$ and the connectedness of the algebraic monodromy groups attached to $A/F$.

items.title: Existence of complete singular solutions of the Yamabe equation at prescribed points
items.summary: Let $(M^n,g)$ be smooth, connected and closed, with $n\ge3$, and let $P$ be a prescribed nonempty finite set. We characterize the conformal classes $[g]$ that admit a complete metric of positive constant scalar curvature on $M\setminus P$. Such a metric exists precisely when $Y(M,[g])>0$ and either $[g]$ is nonround or $|P|\ge2$. In a nonround positive conformal class, the metrics can be chosen with Fowler asymptotics and arbitrary fixed ratios of their small asymptotic neck sizes. As the neck sizes tend to zero, every sequence of these metrics has a subsequence converging smoothly away from the punctures to a smooth Yamabe minimizing metric. The construction allows degenerate Yamabe minimizers and arbitrary curvature jets at the prescribed points. For nonempty closed singular sets $Λ\subset M$ with empty interior, we also announce the same existence criterion with the additional requirement that the Bessel capacity $C_{1+2/n,n/2}(Λ)$ vanish.

items.title: From Numbers to Container Strings
items.summary: We examine two ways of coding sequences in arithmetical theories. We investigate under what conditions they work. To be more precise, we study the creation of objects of a data-type that we call container strings, roughly sequences where the components are ordered but where we do not have an explicitly given projection function and length function. The first coding idea is Smullyan coding and the second one is Markov coding. This second idea is based on the representation of binary strings in the special linear monoid of the non-negative part of discretely ordered commutative rings. We employ Markov coding to obtain an alternative proof that the weak theory ${\sf PA}^-$ is sequential. We prove a correspondence result for a principle for container strings to Euclidean Division under the Markov translation.

items.title: Nonpolynomial entire solutions of the special Lagrangian equation with critical phase
items.summary: In this paper, we construct smooth nonpolynomial entire solutions of the special Lagrangian equation with critical phase $(n-2)π/2$ for every $n\ge4$. Together with the nonquadratic example in dimension two and Warren's example in dimension three, our construction shows that the supercritical condition $|θ|>(n-2)π/2$ in the Bernstein theorem proved by Yuan is sharp in every dimension $n\ge2$.

items.title: Limit laws for Siegel theta sums
items.summary: Siegel theta sums are exponential sums over the integer lattice whose phases are determined by a quadratic form. For a random choice of quadratic form, we prove a limit law for the modulus of the normalised sum as the summation range tends to infinity. The limiting distribution depends on the space from which the quadratic form is sampled. We prove precise heavy-tail asymptotics for random sampling from (a) the full space of quadratic forms and (b) the space of diagonal forms. This study extends classic results by Jurkat and Van Horne for one-variable theta sums and by Götze and Gordin for theta series on Siegel half-spaces. Our approach uses the Shale--Weil representation of the metaplectic group and the ergodic theory of unipotent flows.

items.title: Selecting $2 \times 2$ submatrices with optimally bounded inverses
items.summary: For a matrix $U \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times k}$ ($n \ge k$) with orthonormal columns, the Goreinov--Tyrtyshnikov--Zamarashkin (GTZ) conjecture asserts that there exists a $k \times k$ submatrix $U_I$ with $\|U_I^{-1}\|_2 \le \sqrt{n}$. The conjecture remains open for $3 \le k \le n - 3$. The existence of such a submatrix in the case $k = 2$ was proved for $n=4$ by Nesterenko (2023) and recently for general $n$ by Sengupta and Pautov (2026). In this paper, we give a short, elementary, constructive proof of a weighted strengthening of this result, which yields a single-pass streaming algorithm that selects a row pair satisfying the $\sqrt{n}$ bound in $\mathcal O(n)$ operations and $\mathcal O(1)$ auxiliary memory. We further give an explicit matrix representation of all equality cases for $k = 2$ characterized by Nesterenko (2026) and use it to construct a single matrix family on which standard selection strategies (including global and local maximum-volume selection, Bischof--Stewart pivoted QR, column-pivoted QR, and LU with partial pivoting) simultaneously fail to attain the $\sqrt{n}$ bound.

items.title: On dual varieties of smooth projective varieties
items.summary: For a smooth irreducible nondegenerate complex projective variety $X\subsetneq\mathbb P^N$, we prove that its projective dual $X^\vee$ is a hypersurface whenever $\operatorname{dim} X\ge3\operatorname{codim}X-2$. This result may be regarded as further evidence for Hartshorne's complete intersection conjecture. We also prove the duality defect conjecture of Landman in codimension at most five. Finally, we complete Ein's classification of smooth nondegenerate complex projective varieties with smooth projective dual. The list consists of smooth quadrics, the Segre varieties $\mathbb P^1\times\mathbb P^m$ with $m\ge2$, the Grassmannian $\operatorname{Gr}(2,5)$, and the spinor tenfold in $\mathbb P^{15}$.

items.title: The inductive Galois-McKay conjecture for groups of Lie type C
items.summary: We prove the inductive Galois-McKay conjecture for the symplectic groups. A key result is the determination of the character fields of the irreducible characters of the extensions of the symplectic group by field automorphisms. Two main ingredients for this are the theory of Brauer trees and the generalized Gelfand-Graev characters.

items.title: Efficient Data Fusion in Distributionally Robust Optimization
items.summary: Decisions under uncertainty increasingly rest on fragmented evidence, such as samples from related but different populations, privacy-protected summary statistics, or complementary statistical descriptions of the same data. Distributionally robust optimization (DRO) can fuse such evidence by constructing one ambiguity set per source and hedging against all distributions in the intersection of these sets. This fusion approach is less conservative than aggregating the sources into a single ambiguity set, but it is computationally demanding. Exact reformulations grow exponentially with the number of sources, and even deciding whether the intersection is nonempty is NP-hard. We show that fusion DRO admits an exact reformulation in which the ambiguity sets are coupled only through functional Lagrange multipliers. Restricting these multipliers to affine decision rules yields upper bounds that decompose across the ambiguity sets, are exact for quadratic losses over Wasserstein balls around Gaussian references, and provably dominate aggregation-based relaxations such as Minkowski sums and balls around mixtures. The approximations admit finite conic reformulations in important special cases and subgradient methods for weakly convex losses, which makes fusion DRO applicable to neural network training. In portfolio, newsvendor, and binary classification experiments, the affine approximation stays close to the exact value wherever the latter is computable, scales far better than exact methods, and outperforms aggregation-based benchmarks out-of-sample.

items.title: The Monge Optimal Transport Barycenter Problem with Adaptive Features
items.summary: The data-driven Monge optimal transport barycenter problem seeks a map $y=T(x,z)$ that minimally perturbs an outcome $x$ while removing its statistical dependence on covariates $z$. Numerical implementations approximate the independence constraint through finite-dimensional test-function spaces, making the effectiveness of dependence removal sensitive to the choice of features. This article develops a procedure whereby the features themselves are optimized throughout the procedure. In particular, we adopt a feature space for $f$ consisting of Gaussian radial basis functions (RBFs) with adaptive individual centers and bandwidths. Synthetic experiments show that while fixed nonlinear RBF features can capture dependence structures that are poorly represented by linear features, adapting the RBF centers and bandwidths can further improve dependence removal within a limited feature space and achieve residual dependence comparable to that obtained with a larger fixed basis. We further extend the formulation to multidimensional covariates and evaluate its applicability to real-world problems, including removing age-related dependence in biomedical measurements and dependence on temperature and humidity in bike-sharing demand.

items.title: Exact sequences of regular LF-spaces
items.summary: We show that the category of regular LF-spaces has all kernels but, unlike the category of regular LB-spaces, does not have all cokernels. Its topological exact structure, maximal exact structure and maximal deflation-exact structure form a strictly increasing chain of proper subclasses of the class of all kernel-cokernel pairs. To the best of the authors' knowledge, regular LF-spaces in particular provide the first natural example of a category that has all kernels but is not preabelian and whose maximal deflation-exact structure is neither two-sided exact nor equal to the class of all kernel-cokernel pairs.

items.title: Infinite Hyper-Order of Entire Solutions of a First-Order Differential Equation
items.summary: Let $\varphi$ be a transcendental entire function of finite order. We prove that every entire solution of $$g'=e^\varphi g+1$$ has infinite hyper-order. Then we prove the Brück's conjecture.

items.title: The Riemann hypothesis
items.summary: The Weyl symbolic calculus of operators leads to the construction, if one takes for symbol a certain distribution decomposing over the zeros of the Riemann zeta function, of an operator with the following property: the Riemann hypothesis is equivalent to the validity of a collection of estimates involving this operator. Pseudodifferential arithmetic, a novel chapter of pseudodifferential operator theory, makes it possible to make the operator under study fully explicit. This leads to a proof of the conjecture.

items.title: Equal probabilities maximize the expected deficit in the siblings of the coupon collector
items.summary: In the siblings (or brotherhood) variant of the coupon collector's problem, a main collector draws coupons until her own album is complete and passes every duplicate down a chain of siblings; the $j$th collector is then left with $U_j^N$ empty places, $j\ge 2$. It has been conjectured [stated as an open problem in the work that introduced the model] that, for every fixed number of coupon types $N$ and every $j\ge 2$, the expected deficit $\E[U_j^N]$ is maximized by the equiprobable coupon distribution. We prove this in a sharp, finite-$N$ form: $\E[U_j^N]$ is strictly larger at the uniform vector than at any other probability vector, and indeed strictly increases along every ray running from an arbitrary distribution toward the uniform one. The proof is exact and elementary in its ingredients. An inclusion--exclusion step turns the governing Poissonized integral into a one-dimensional integral with a separable integrand; a single integration by parts then rewrites the radial derivative of $\E[U_j^N]$ as a positively weighted covariance of an increasing function, whose sign is settled by Chebyshev's correlation inequality. We show that $\E[U_j^N]$ is \emph{not} Schur-concave, so that no majorization or pairwise-smoothing argument can yield the result, and we explain why the recent variance-extremality method of Long~[Long, arXiv:2604.25108, 2026] does not transfer. As by-products we obtain a finite closed form for $\E[U_j^N]$ over subsets of the coupon set and the exact Hessian of $\E[U_j^N]$ at the uniform vector. The argument extends without change to all real $j>1$.

items.title: Full-chip constrained quantum annealing via self-calibrating spin-susceptibility control
items.summary: Discrete optimization in finance, power grids, and logistics requires minimizing Ising Hamiltonians under coupled linear constraints. However, quadratic-penalty formulations superimpose dense cliques that exhaust the minor-embedding capacity of sparse superconducting processors at 128-176 spins, and first-order dual subgradient schemes diverge or stall under constraint coupling. Accordingly, this study proposes a hardware-native quantum-classical closed-loop primal-dual workflow, designated as Self-Calibrating Quantum Susceptibility Quasi-Newton (SelfCal-QSQN), in which linear constraints are encoded in longitudinal fields with zero auxiliary quadratic penalty couplings and dual curvature is reconstructed from single-shot spin-fluctuation covariances. This workflow requires no slack qubits or perturbation queries. Evaluated over 891 runs on D-Wave Advantage (5,612 qubits) and Advantage2 (4,560 qubits), SelfCal-QSQN drives the pre-polish trajectory-minimum raw QPU sample violation to $0.108 \pm 0.017$ at 4,560 qubits (83.3% exact feasibility after a deterministic 1-bit polish with best-incumbent tracking, reaching 47.3% of the continuous linear-programming relaxation bound), reduces high-constraint error by 6.1- to 20.1-fold over K-scaled first-order updates, attains 5.35-fold deeper feasible energies than linear programming with the identical 1-bit polish within a 4.10-s compute-only budget at 256 spins, and achieves 95.0%-96.7% feasibility on non-native and inequality benchmarks. Moreover, the workflow is robust toward shot noise and freeze-out drift.

items.title: Existence of odd-frequency free boundary points in the Signorini problem
items.summary: Up to a lower-dimensional set, the free boundary of the Signorini problem consists of points with frequency that is half-integer, even (at zero density points), or odd (at full density points). Surprisingly, despite extensive work on the structure and regularity of each of these sets, the existence of odd-frequency free boundary points has remained open. In this paper, we construct a solution with a free boundary point of frequency 3.

items.title: Global Convergence of Second-Order Methods for Physics-Informed Neural Networks in the Overparameterized Limit
items.summary: Solving high-dimensional partial differential equations (PDEs) constitutes a core task in many engineering and scientific disciplines. Physics-informed neural networks and the deep Galerkin method effectively leverage machine learning models to approximate solutions of known PDEs by minimizing residuals corresponding to the PDE operator alongside external constraints. Although second-order optimizers are becoming increasingly popular for training neural networks (NNs) to solve PDEs and empirically outperform their first-order counterparts in both speed and accuracy, the convergence theory for training such models is essentially confined to first-order methods. In this paper, we close this gap and develop a convergence analysis for the regularized Newton and Gauss-Newton methods. As the number of hidden units tends to infinity, the training dynamics converge in probability, with explicit rates, to the solution of a deterministic limit equation involving a Newton neural tangent kernel operator associated with the PDE. Although the limiting kernel operator admits no spectral gap, we prove that, in the overparameterized limit, the PDE residual vanishes as training proceeds, and, under mild assumptions, the NN converges to the PDE solution. We further show that, provided a sufficiently small regularization parameter, the projection of the residual onto any fixed number of leading eigenfunctions decays exponentially fast, demonstrating that this hyperparameter acts as a spectral filter: it lifts the convergence rates of high-frequency components toward those of low-frequency ones, thereby mitigating the spectral bias inherent in gradient descent. Mathematical challenges arise from the implicit parameter update involving a linear system whose dimension increases with the NN width and, for Newton's method, a potentially indefinite Hessian, as well as from the PDE operator entering the kernel.

items.title: Prandtl Batchelor flow in a Periodic Channel with Counter Moving Walls
items.summary: We study the vanishing viscosity limit of steady two dimensional incompressible Navier Stokes flows in a horizontally periodic channel with counter moving walls. The prescribed wall velocities are small periodic perturbations of constant velocities with opposite signs. The Batchelor Wood relations select an affine Euler shear with constant vorticity and a unique interior zero. We establish the existence of steady Navier Stokes solutions that are uniformly approximated by the selected Euler shear together with two Prandtl boundary layers. Moreover, the vorticity converges locally uniformly to the selected constant vorticity. The principal analytical difficulty is the loss of global coercivity caused by the interior zero of the Euler shear. To overcome this difficulty, we develop a compactness rigidity argument that combines signed near wall positivity estimates, interior vorticity estimates, adjoint tests eliminating the affine limiting modes, and a streamline circulation equation ruling out concentration near the walls. These ingredients yield an estimate for the linearized inverse, which, together with a high order Euler Prandtl approximation, enables us to solve the nonlinear error equations. Our result provides a rigorous realization of the Prandtl Batchelor selection principle in a periodic channel with counter moving walls.

items.title: A Geometric Derivation of the Einstein Equations from the Causal Action Principle
items.summary: The causal action principle for causal fermion systems is analyzed for a minimizing measure whose support is assumed to have the structure of a smooth manifold $\tilde{M}$. The concept of osculating vacua is introduced. It is shown that the Lagrangian induces on $\tilde{M}$ a Lorentzian metric. Moreover, the Euler-Lagrange equations of the causal action imply that the Ricci tensor must satisfy the Einstein equations of General Relativity for an energy-momentum tensor given in terms of a power expansion in the regularization length. The gravitational coupling constant is found to be the square of the regularization length. Our methods provide a systematic procedure for deriving corrections to the Einstein equations. The paper includes a self-contained introduction to causal variational principles and the causal action principle. Most geometric structures (connection, Riemannian metric and curvature) are introduced and analyzed in the general setting of causal variational principles for an arbitrary dimension of $\tilde{M}$. The Lorentzian setting works only for causal fermion systems and is worked out only in four spacetime dimensions.

items.title: Separation points and pressure gradients for the nonstationary Stokes system with localized boundary data in the half-space
items.summary: We study separation points of the nonstationary Stokes system in a half-space with zero initial data and nonnegative, space-time separable boundary data supported in the unit ball and in $[0,1]$, respectively. A separation point is a pair $(x',t)$, with $x'$ outside the spatial support, arbitrarily near which a velocity component takes both signs. The main ingredient is an explicit representation of the velocity and pressure via confluent hypergeometric functions. For normal boundary data, if the temporal boundary data are regular and unimodal, log-concavity yields a unique separation time for the $i$th tangential component at every boundary point with $|x_i|>1$, and exactly two for the normal component at distant points, one before and one after the boundary data vanish. The later one, a simple zero of the second normal derivative of the normal component at the boundary, is unique even without unimodality. We obtain monotonicity and asymptotics of separation times and vanishing rates of normal derivatives. For tangential boundary data with $n\geq3$, under the same assumptions, a separation time for the velocity component in their direction exists at $x'$ with $|x'|>1$ precisely when the corresponding Riesz transform of the spatial boundary data has a positive derivative in that direction at $x'$, and log-concavity makes it unique. For the remaining components, we prove existence and uniqueness of separation points on distant lines parallel to the axes, with asymptotics in terms of spatial moments and support geometry. For radial spatial boundary data, we determine the signs and zero sets of tangential pressure derivatives.

items.title: Counting Classical Fullerenes VII: Arithmetic Unranking of Fullerene Isomers
items.summary: Given a vertex number $2m$ and a rank, we construct the corresponding ordinary fullerene as a planar adjacency list. Choosing the rank uniformly therefore samples ordinary isomorphism classes exactly from the vertex number alone. We select an integral period by counting lattice points on a quadratic level in polytopes with fixed facet directions. For a fixed positive semidefinite integral form on a box of radius $H$, with a linear term of coefficients $O(H)$, the algorithm computes all level counts simultaneously in $O(H^2\operatorname{polylog}(2m))$ bit operations when $H=O(\sqrt m)$ and the facet offsets have $O(\log(2m))$ bits. A signed decomposition into orthogonal simplices gives this bound. For fullerenes we use deterministic $O(m^2\operatorname{polylog}(2m))$ bit work to construct an index of $O(m\log(2m))$ bits. With this index a rank costs $O(m\operatorname{polylog}(2m))$ bit work, uniformly in the rank. Two families of recuts let energy descent escape self-contacts in the slit polygon. The decoder then writes the graph from its selected period in $O(m)$ arithmetic word operations.

items.title: $E_d$-Enhancements of $L_\infty$-Algebras Associated to Secondary Polytopes
items.summary: We study $E_d$-enhancements of the geometric $L_\infty$-algebras associated to secondary polytopes of finite configurations in $\mathbb R^d$, $d\geq2$. We construct an action of the semialgebraic chains of the Fulton--MacPherson operad on the shifted algebra $B_A=\mathfrak g_A[1-d]$ when $|A|\leq3d$. The action recovers the prescribed higher Lie operations on fundamental chains. The construction is obtained from a general extension theorem for weighted shifted $L_\infty$-algebras, using reflection to control relative cohomology obstructions. For $|A|\leq3d-1$, the resulting reflection-compatible integration actions are homotopic relative to their shifted Lie structure. We also give an abstract enhancement without a cardinality bound, direct formulas for circuits, and explicit operations for convex pentagons and hexagons.

items.title: 1-Laplacian type problems with strongly singular nonlinearities and gradient terms
items.summary: We show optimal existence, nonexistence and regularity results for nonnegative solutions to Dirichlet problems as $$ \begin{cases} \displaystyle -Δ_1 u = g(u)|D u|+h(u)f & \text{in}\;Ω,\\ u=0 & \text{on}\;\partialΩ, \end{cases} $$ where $Ω$ is an open bounded subset of $\mathbb{R}^N$, $f\geq 0$ belongs to $L^N(Ω)$, and $g$ and $h$ are continuous functions that may blow up at zero. As a noteworthy fact we show how a non-trivial interaction mechanism between the two nonlinearities $g$ and $h$ produces remarkable regularizing effects on the solutions. The sharpness of our main results is discussed through the use of appropriate explicit examples.

items.title: Vertex-transitive strongly regular graphs in the switching class of doubly transitive two-graphs
items.summary: Let $\mathcal{T}$ be a finite two-graph whose full automorphism group $G$ is $2$-transitive. Up to complementation, we classify the primitive strongly regular graphs with associated two-graph $\mathcal{T}$ whose full automorphism group is a transitive maximal subgroup of $G$ and does not contain the largest perfect subgroup of $G$. In doing so, we obtain a new family of vertex-transitive strongly regular graphs whose associated two-graph arises from $PΣL(2,q)$.

items.title: Generic vanishing and singularities of theta divisors
items.summary: We study the connection between the generic vanishing conjecture for subvarieties of principally polarized abelian varieties and various predictions about the singularities of theta divisors. We deduce new cases of a conjecture on the multiplicities of points on irreducible theta divisors, as well as Beauville's conjecture characterizing Jacobians by the size of their theta singularity loci.

items.title: Counting Classical Fullerenes I: Exact Enumeration and Generic Achiral Symmetry
items.summary: We give an exact arithmetic formula for the number of classical fullerenes on $2m$ vertices. The oriented count is known; the new contribution counts achiral fullerenes, those admitting an orientation-reversing symmetry. We transport these symmetries to a lattice, classify eleven types, and express their contribution as seven weighted orbit counts. The complete formula is printed here, together with an exact algorithm producing all counts through index $M$ in quasilinear bit time with fast integer multiplication. We also prove that the proportion of achiral fullerenes with a unique orientation-reversing symmetry tends to one as the size increases. That symmetry is either a reflection or a fixed-point-free involution, with cumulative proportions $527/529$ and $2/529$. Among all fullerenes on $2m$ vertices, the achiral proportion has order $m^{-5}$; the same order holds cumulatively. The exceptional achiral classes with nontrivial orientation-preserving symmetry number $O(m^2)$.

items.title: The singular Paneitz equation on four-manifolds: refined blow-up analysis and degree jumps
items.summary: We compute the Leray--Schauder degree of the singular Paneitz equation on a closed four-manifold with conical orders strictly between minus one and zero. We assume that the kernel of the Paneitz operator consists of the constants. In each positive nonresonant chamber the degree is a partial sum of an explicit generating series determined by the Euler characteristic and the conical orders. We match the heights of exact blow-up solutions and expand the gradient near the corrected projected bubbles. A localized dilation identity gives its common-scale component on the zero set of the relative-scale equations. For generic data a fixed-mass homotopy then gives the signed degree of each concentrating configuration. Assign ordinary points weight one and conical points weight one plus their order. If the largest concentrating weight exceeds one half, a finite second moment gives the coefficient. At one half the expansion acquires a logarithm, and below one half the coefficient is a global finite part. On the round four-sphere with two antipodal points of equal weight below one half, perturbing the prescribed curvature away from both points selects the side of bubbling.

items.title: Partial $F$-invariants and cluster categorifications
items.summary: The $F$-invariant in cluster algebras is a combinatorial invariant that unifies the $E$-invariant from additive categorification and the $\mathfrak{d}$-invariant from monoidal categorification. In this paper, we study its refinement, the partial $F$-invariant, and establish its mutation formula under changes of the initial seed. As an application, we prove a conjecture of Reading, which asserts that the non-compatible cluster variables can be separated by sign-coherence of $g$-vectors upon varying the initial seed. We further show that, for cluster monomials, the partial $F$-invariants coincide with both the partial $E$-invariants for reachable decorated representations of quivers with potentials and the pole orders of normalized $R$-matrices (or partial $\mathfrak{d}$-invariants) for finite-dimensional reachable simple modules over quantum affine algebras. As consequences, we obtain a combinatorial formula for the pole orders for reachable simple modules in terms of $q$-characters; we verify the conjectural explicit formula for the pole orders between Kirillov--Reshetikhin modules.

items.title: Computing and Optimizing the $H^2$-norm of Delay Differential Algebraic Systems
items.summary: We present a Lanczos tau method for the approximation and optimization of the $H^2$-norm of time-delay systems described by delay differential algebraic equations of index one. The soundness of this approach is proven under the assumption of a finite strong $H^2$-norm. Furthermore, we prove convergence if the rational approximation of the exponential underlying the discretization is well-behaved and the discretization is stability preserving. Numerical results suggest that, for multiple delays, the method converges at cubic rate in the discretization degree for systems of retarded type and linearly for those of neutral type. In the single delay case, we note geometric convergence of the $H^2$-norm for systems of both retarded and neutral type when a symmetric basis is chosen. Explicit formulas are derived for the gradient of the approximation with respect to system parameters and delays. These allow us to compute the entire gradient using only about double the computational time of approximating the $H^2$-norm alone. We illustrate how these can be used to synthesize robust feedback controllers and stable approximate models. The article is concluded by a discussion of how the presented results extend and improve for approximations based on splines. We note acceleration of the convergence rate by a little over a full order for such a choice. Finally, we prove that a Lanczos tau method using a spline based on Legendre orthogonal polynomials preserves stability and guarantees convergence of the $H^2$-norm.

items.title: Decision-Focused Learning for Multistage Stochastic Programs, with Application to Power Network Repair Scheduling
items.summary: Multistage stochastic programs (MSPs) with discrete decisions are hard to solve due to the curse of dimensionality, non-convex value functions, and scenario trees that grow exponentially with the horizon. We develop a decision-focused learning (DFL) framework for MSPs in which a neural network predicts scores for the part of the decision that drives the state transition. Under structural conditions that make this sub-decision enter the stage objective linearly, the network is trained on labels from offline single-scenario problems, using the Fenchel-Young loss with perturbed optimizers, which need only an optimization oracle. We apply the framework to repair scheduling in power networks under stochastic, time-varying component failures, with and without a per-stage repair budget. On a synthetic 5-bus network and on the IEEE 14-bus network at two repair-cost scales, the learned and baseline policies are compared on common evaluation paths. Without the budget, DFL is the cheapest policy on the 5-bus network; on the 14-bus network it does not outperform a near-sighted model-predictive control (MPC) baseline, but it beats repairing every failed component at the higher scale. Under a binding budget, DFL is the cheapest policy evaluated on both networks and at both scales, 14% to 23% below the next-best policy. On the 5-bus network, the mean cost of DFL is 1.7% (without the budget) and 1.8% (with it) above the exact optimum computed by dynamic programming. Within days of computation, sample average approximation yields costlier policies than DFL and the repair-everything heuristic, and stochastic dual dynamic integer programming remains far from convergence. DFL computes its decisions about as fast as the trivial heuristics and orders of magnitude faster than MPC. Since these conditions are not specific to power networks, the framework extends to other MSPs that share this structure.

items.title: Homogenization with Shape-Evolving Microstructures: A Two-Phase Membrane Problem
items.summary: We study a diffusion problem in a highly heterogeneous periodic medium (characterized by a small scale parameter $0<\varepsilon\ll1$) where small inclusions are separated from the surrounding connected area by solute-impermeable membranes. These membranes are allowed to grow and deform under surface tension and osmotic pressure (driven by the concentration difference across the membrane). We prove existence of weak solutions on a time interval which is independent of the microscopic scale via a Schauder fixed-point argument by establishing spatial boundary Hölder estimates. For the homogenization limit $\varepsilon\to0$, we establish strong compactness of the outer concentration via time translates and then derive a stability estimate for the driven inner cell problems. The limit couples a macroscopic conservation law, with shape-dependent effective diffusion, to inner diffusion and membrane motion in each cell.

items.title: Concave shifts and the complete Nevanlinna--Pick property
items.summary: Let $\mathcal{H}$ be a non-zero reproducing kernel Hilbert space of holomorphic functions on the unit disc, and assume $\mathcal{H}$ is invariant under the forward and backward shifts. We show that if the forward shift on $\mathcal{H}$ is concave, then $\mathcal{H}$ is a complete Nevanlinna--Pick (CNP) space. This answers a question by Shimorin, and greatly extends his result that any space of Dirichlet type is CNP. As a byproduct of our investigation, we also show that if the forward shift on $\mathcal{H}$ is concave, then any multiplier of $\mathcal{H}$ is the SOT limit of its Cesàro means. As applications, we prove a commutant lifting theorem for concave cyclic analytic operators, and several results about shift-invariant subspaces in de~Branges--Rovnyak spaces.

items.title: Preserving Ramsey ultrafilters with tree forcings
items.summary: We define a wide class of tree forcings that we call $\textit{normed-tree forcings}$ and prove that they can preserve Ramsey ultrafilters. These include $\textit{fat-tree forcings}$ as particular cases. As an application, we prove the consistency with $\mathsf{ZFC}$ of $\mathfrak{d}=\mathfrak{u}=\aleph_1 < \mathsf{minLc}=\mathfrak{c}=\aleph_2$, where $\mathfrak{d}$ denotes the dominating number, $\mathfrak{u}$ the ultrafilter number, and $\mathsf{minLc}$ the minimum localization cardinal. This solves some open questions about pairs of classical cardinal characteristics, such as the consistency of both $\mathfrak{e}_{\mathsf{ubd}}$ and its dual strictly larger than $\mathfrak{u}$.

items.title: Galois scalar extension of simple Lie algebras
items.summary: We investigate the behaviour of simple finite-dimensional Lie algebras under finite Galois field extensions. Given a simple Lie algebra $L$ over a field $\mathbb{F}$ and a finite Galois extension $\mathbb{K}/\mathbb{F}$ of degree $n = [\mathbb{K}:\mathbb{F}]$, we prove that if $L$ is isomorphic to a $\mathbb{K}$-Lie algebra $S$ viewed as an $\mathbb{F}$-algebra, then the scalar extension $L \otimes_{\mathbb{F}} \mathbb{K}$ is isomorphic to the direct sum of $n$ copies of $S$. Furthermore, for cyclic extensions of order a prime number, we show that if no such $\mathbb{K}$-Lie algebra $S$ exists, the extended algebra $L \otimes_{\mathbb{F}} \mathbb{K}$ remains simple. This framework provides a general mechanism to transfer structural and classification results across different ground fields. In addition, we examine the centroids of simple Lie algebras, proving that the dimension of the space of centroids is invariant under finite field extensions. As an application, we explicitly determine the structure of the spaces of centroids for simple Lie algebras over finite fields.

items.title: Morse theory and a degree formula for the resonant singular Paneitz equation on four-manifolds
items.summary: We develop Morse theory for the singular Paneitz equation at resonant mass on closed four-manifolds with conical orders between minus one and zero and Paneitz kernel consisting of the constants. Under nondegeneracy of the reduced interactions and nonvanishing of the leading mass-defect coefficients, we classify the critical points at infinity by the sign of these coefficients. We compute their indices and their contributions to the relative homology of sublevels. The topology of very low sublevels is determined by weighted barycenters of strictly smaller total weight and by the negative Paneitz eigenspace. These results yield strong Morse inequalities and a Leray--Schauder degree formula at resonance, which also applies when genuine solutions are degenerate. On the round four-sphere with two conical points, the Morse inequalities give existence on an open set of data for which the degree vanishes.

items.title: Properties of f correlated fuzzy numbers
items.summary: This paper investigates structural invariance and algebraic classification properties within the theory of interactive fuzzy numbers, focusing on $f$-correlated and more specifically, linearly correlated fuzzy numbers. Starting from the foundations of joint possibility distributions and the generalized extension principle, we analyze how continuous, strictly monotonic correlation functions $f$ act on $α$-level sets and membership representations. We prove that $f$-correlation preserves the class $\mathcal{F}_C(\mathbb{R})$ of fuzzy numbers with continuous endpoints and transforms any $L$-$R$ fuzzy number into a generalized $L_f$-$R_f$ (or $R_f$-$L_f$) fuzzy number, with explicit formulas for the induced shape functions. Specializing to hyperbolic correlation ($f(x) = q/x + r$) illustrates how nonlinear interactivity preserves generalized $L$-$R$ regularity while deforming piecewise-linear triangular and trapezoidal flanks into rational curves. In contrast, when $f(x) = qx + r$ is affine, the reference shape functions $(L, R)$ are preserved up to orientation reversal, yielding complete set-theoretic characterizations of the $A$-linearly correlated spaces $\mathbb{R}_{\mathcal{F}(A)}$ for symmetric Gaussian, trapezoidal, and triangular generators, as well as necessary and sufficient shape-ratio conditions for linear correlation in the asymmetric setting.

items.title: Non-Intrusive Least-Squares Reduced Basis Methods: Black-Box Snapshots and Exact Residual Certificates
items.summary: For a parametrized linear first-order system, the least-squares functional at a conforming pair is the squared norm of the residual of the continuous problem, and it can be computed exactly. In this paper, we use this least-squares residual as the error certificate of reduced basis methods whose snapshots are computed by black-box solvers. The output of the solver is first made conforming by a reconstruction, and a flux is recovered by least-squares if the solver does not provide one. The online reduced problem minimizes the least-squares functional over the product of the space spanned by the snapshot fluxes and the space spanned by the snapshot potentials. It needs no inf--sup condition on the reduced spaces, and its certificate needs no stability constant. We discuss second-order elliptic equations, the Stokes equations, where only the velocity of a black-box solver is used, and linear transport equations with a moving inflow boundary. In the numerical experiments, the snapshots are computed by least-squares, conforming, nonconforming, stabilized, finite volume, and finite difference solvers. With adaptive meshes and the same tolerances, the greedy algorithm stops at the same or nearly the same reduced dimension for all solvers that accept a mesh.

items.title: On Frobenius-Schur exponent bounds
items.summary: We study bounds on the Frobenius--Schur exponent of spherical fusion categories in terms of their global dimension, generalizing bounds from the representation theory of finite-dimensional quasi-Hopf algebras. Our main result is that if the Frobenius--Schur exponent of a modular fusion category is a power of a prime $p$, then it is bounded by the norm of its global dimension when $p$ is odd, and by four times the norm of its global dimension when $p=2$; these bounds are optimal. Moreover, it is bounded by a constant multiple of the geometric mean of the Galois conjugates of its global dimension, which is much smaller when the global dimension is irrational, and a bound of this type is proven for each prime power dividing the Frobenius--Schur exponent of an arbitrary modular or spherical fusion category. Under pseudounitarity, we describe all modular and spherical fusion categories whose Frobenius--Schur exponent is a prime power and at least the norm (respectively, the square of the norm) of their global dimension, using a classification of modular fusion categories of Frobenius--Perron dimension $p^n$ for $n\leq5$.

items.title: Stability of separable solutions to a fast diffusion system
items.summary: We study a Dirichlet fast diffusion system with symmetric linear cross-loss terms on a bounded smooth domain. A coupled Rayleigh quotient captures the variational structure of the coupling and is nonincreasing along sufficiently regular positive solution pairs. Under the common extinction and regularity hypotheses, this monotonicity and the energy identity yield upper and lower bounds \[ C^{-1}(T^*-t)^{1/(p-1)} \le \|(u(t),v(t))\|_{L^{p+1}(Ω)} \le C(T^*-t)^{1/(p-1)}. \] In the Sobolev subcritical range, a Lyapunov functional for the rescaled system yields a sequence of times $t_j\uparrow T^*$ along which the rescaled pair converges strongly in $H_0^1(Ω)\times H_0^1(Ω)$ to a nonnegative classical stationary solution pair. The integral lower bound excludes the trivial limiting pair, while the coupling with $α>0$ ensures that neither limiting component is identically zero. As a further property of the stationary system, we show that proportional components of a nontrivial nonnegative solution pair must coincide. We also construct a positive diagonal stationary solution pair by constrained minimization. Scalar upper comparison and a Bénilan--Crandall-type estimate for smooth positive diagonal solutions provide complementary links with the scalar fast diffusion equation.

items.title: Stability of 3D Stratified Plane Couette Flow: A New Lift-up Mechanism and Potential Vorticity
items.summary: Since the pioneering work of Taylor and Goldstein in 1931 laid the foundation for the study of parallel stratified shear flows, non-parallel configurations have received comparatively little attention. We study the stability of the 3D Boussinesq system near the plane Couette flow $V^*=(y,0,0)$ under the vertically stratified background $η^*=αz$. The shear and stratification directions are perpendicular. This geometry produces two structural effects that are absent in the parallel configuration: an additional nonlocal coupling in the non-zero-mode system, which obstructs a directly useful symmetrization, and a wave-shear coupled lift-up mechanism for the zero modes. The transient growth due to the lift-up effect can be suppressed either by sufficiently strong stratification or under suitable assumptions on the initial data. To study the nonzero-mode system, we introduce a reformulation based on the linearized potential vorticity (PV), a fundamental quantity in geophysical fluid dynamics, to recover a better energy structure. We establish the inviscid damping of $u_{1,\neq}$ and $u_{2,\neq}$. We further apply the linearized PV formulation to study the linear stability of the tilted Couette flow. Finally, we use this formulation to prove the nonlinear stability for perturbations on $\mathbb{T}\times\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{T}$ and show that strong stratification can enhance the stability.

items.title: A very short proof of Sidorenko's inequality for counts of homomorphism between graphs
items.summary: A fundamental extremality result due to Sidorenko (Discrete Math. 131.1-3, 1994) states that among all connected graphs G on k vertices, the k-vertex star maximises the number of graph homomorphisms of G into any graph H. We provide a new short proof of this result using only a simple recursive counting argument for trees and Hölder's inequality.

items.title: A Solution Concept for Convex Vector Optimization Problems based on a User-defined Region of Interest
items.summary: This work addresses arbitrary convex vector optimization problems, which constitute a general framework for multi-criteria decision-making in diverse real-world applications. Due to their complexity, such problems are typically tackled using polyhedral approximation. Existing solution concepts rely on additional assumptions, such as boundedness, polyhedrality of the ordering cone, or existence of interior points in the ordering cone, and typically focus on absolute error measures. We introduce a solution concept based on the homogenization of the upper image that employs relative error measures and avoids additional structural assumptions. Although minimality is not explicitly required, a form of approximate weak minimality is implicitly ensured under attainability. The concept is straightforward, requiring only a single precision parameter and, owing to relative errors, remains robust under scaling of the target functions. Homogenization also eliminates the need for the binary distinction between points far from the origin and directions which can lead to numerical difficulties. Furthermore, in practice decision-makers often identify a region where preferred solutions are expected. Our concept supports both a global overview of the upper image and a refined local perspective within such a user-defined region of interest (RoI). We present a decision-making procedure enabling iterative refinement of this region and the associated preferences.

items.title: Ultrarank and ideal structure of uniform Roe algebras
items.summary: In this paper, we study the ideal structure of the uniform Roe algebra $C^*_u(X)$ for a coarse disjoint union $X = \bigsqcup_{n\in\mathbb{N}} X_n$ of finite metric spaces, with a focus on ideals lying between the compact ideal $\mathcal{K}$ and the ghost ideal $\mathcal{G}$. To analyze these ideals, we introduce a nonstandard invariant called the $\varepsilon$-ultrarank of an operator, which is stable under compact perturbations and completely characterizes principal ideal inclusions in the block-diagonal Calkin algebra. Using the $\varepsilon$-ultrarank as an obstruction to ideal inclusion in $C^*_u(X)$, we construct an ideal between $\mathcal{K}$ and $\mathcal{G}$ that cannot be written as the intersection of any geometric ideal and the ghost ideal. On the positive side, when the averaging projection $P$ belongs to $C^*_u(X)$, we prove that the closed two-sided ideal $\langle P \rangle$ generated by $P$ equals $\mathcal{G}$ if and only if every ghost operator has finite ultrarank and $X$ has zero-density Property A, and we classify all closed two-sided ideals of $C^*_u(X)$ in this case.

items.title: Optimal bounds for $(n,t,w,w-2)$-constant-power error-correcting cooling codes
items.summary: High temperatures have dramatic negative effects on interconnect performance. In a bus, whenever a wire changes its state from ``0'' to ``1'' or from ``1'' to ``0'', Joule heating causes the temperature to rise. Constant-power error-correcting cooling (CPECC) codes, introduced in [IEEE Trans. Inf. Theory, 66 (2020), 4804--4818], are coding schemes that can simultaneously control the peak temperature and the average power consumption of on-chip buses while providing error-correction capability for transmitted information. This paper establishes a new upper bound for $(n,t,w,w-2)$-CPECC codes for $t<w-3$ by some graph-theoretic techniques and the probabilistic method, and constructs several new families of optimal CPECC codes using the asymptotic existence result for GDDs. For $t\geq w-3$, this paper also provides a new upper bound for $(n,t,w,w-2)$-CPECC codes by some hypergraph-theoretic techniques, and several new families of CPECC codes attaining the resulting upper bounds using RBIBDs. The previous upper bound for $(n,t,w,w-2)$-CPECC codes in [arXiv:2608.08742] is a special case of our upper bound.

items.title: Brunn-Minkowski inequalities for chord integrals
items.summary: Chord integrals are moments of chord lengths and translation-invariant averages of dual quermassintegrals. In this paper, we prove their Brunn-Minkowski inequality for $q\in[1,n+2]\cup\{n+3\}$, with equality precisely for homothetic bodies. A transfer from symmetric dual quermassintegrals to covariogram level sets gives, in dimension two, the full range $1\leq q\leq5$. For every $0<q<1$, we establish the same inequality for simplices and an explicit factor version for all convex bodies. On the other hand, rectangular perturbations give counterexamples for every $q>n+1+β_*$, where $β_*\in(2,3)$. As consequences, we obtain Minkowski inequalities and uniqueness results for chord measures. We also prove Brunn-Minkowski inequalities for affine-section integrals and mixed Riesz energies.

items.title: Fixed Points and Envelope Dynamics on Credal Hyperspaces
items.summary: Let $X$ be a compact metric space and consider the hyperspace $\mathscr C_X$ of nonempty weakly closed convex sets of Borel probability measures on $X$, called credal sets. These sets represent uncertainty about which probability law governs the phenomenon of interest. We equip $\mathscr C_X$ with the Hausdorff metric induced by a metric for weak convergence. Credal order intervals $[\mathcal{A},\mathcal{B}] = \{ \mathcal{P}\in\mathscr C_X: \mathcal{A}\subseteq\mathcal{P}\subseteq\mathcal{B} \}$ are complete lattices, and every inclusion-monotone, Hausdorff-continuous self map of such an interval has least and greatest fixed points obtained as limits of iteration from $\mathcal{A}$ and $\mathcal{B}$. For families of inclusion-monotone updates that may vary with time, we construct lower and upper envelope maps that bound every admissible trajectory. When these envelope maps are Hausdorff-continuous, the distance of every trajectory from a limiting credal interval vanishes uniformly over all switching sequences and initial credal sets. Coalescence of the limiting interval endpoints yields convergence to a common credal limit. We then construct the credal evolution induced by a time consistent Nisio semigroup. Uniform $W_1$ contraction of the underlying Markov semigroups induces Hausdorff-Wasserstein contraction of the credal evolution, yielding a unique common invariant credal set, exponential convergence from every initial credal set, and a support functional equal to the robust ergodic limit. We also derive perturbation bounds from finite time Nisio discrepancies and one step kernel set discrepancies, and characterize the countable sequences of support coordinates that represent credal sets, providing an explicit reconstruction formula.

items.title: On Bramble-Pasciak-type preconditioners and their properties
items.summary: Bramble and Pasciak (Math. Comp., 1988) discovered a preconditioning method for linear algebraic systems in saddle point form, which under certain conditions transforms a symmetric indefinite saddle point matrix into a nonsymmetric matrix that is positive definite in some non-standard inner product. Thus, the method "removes" the indefiniteness of the problem, while retaining the property that the preconditioned system can be solved using an optimal Krylov subspace method with three-term recurrences. Since this well-known method has some limitations, several variants with potential improvements have been proposed in the literature. In this paper, we attempt a systematic assessment of the mathematical properties and practical efficiency of Bramble-Pasciak-type preconditioners. Our goal is to close some gaps in the understanding of these techniques. We identify and analyze the three main methods in this context, highlighting a variant that offers additional flexibility but has received little attention to date. We perform detailed spectral analyzes of the preconditioned matrices and illustrate our theoretical results on several numerical examples.

items.title: The exterior Dirichlet problem for the Weingarten equation
items.summary: We solve the exterior Dirichlet problem for the Weingarten equation of minimal type over the complementary of domains satisfying an interior sphere condition, and investigate some related problems. Namely, by linearizing the Weingarten equation, we give an asymptotic expansion for exterior solutions and we completely identify which classes of Weingarten minimal ends satisfy a maximum principle at infinity. Building on the previous results, we study symmetries of the solutions and questions related to the uniqueness of the solutions.

items.title: Aspects of the Livšic Theory for Anosov Endomorphisms
items.summary: The classical Livšic theorem states that a real-valued observable over a transitive hyperbolic system is a coboundary if and only if its sums over all periodic orbits vanish. In this work, we extend this result to the non-invertible setting by establishing a $C^1$ Livšic cohomology theorem for Anosov endomorphisms. We also address the problem of characterizing when SRB measures coincide with inverse SRB measures in this setting. Finally, motivated by rigidity results for Anosov diffeomorphisms, we establish an analogous Livšic--Sinai-type theorem for $C^2$ Anosov endomorphisms. Specifically, we prove that if the restriction of an Anosov endomorphism $f$ to its non-wandering set has the same degree as $f$, and $Jf^n(p)=(°(f))^n$ for every periodic point $p$ of period $n$, then $f$ is transitive and preserves a normalized $C^1$ volume measure.

items.title: Invariant subspaces and nest algebras in left-right operator splitting
items.summary: The left--right (L-R) splitting method for boundary integral equations in rough-surface scattering writes the integral operator as the sum of its lower- and strictly upper- triangular parts. This note examines the operator algebra formed by the lower-triangular ($L$-type) parts.Their weak closure is a nest algebra; second-kind $L$-type operators with Hilbert--Schmidt kernels have $L$-type inverses; and Arveson's distance formula expresses the error of the best possible forward-only approximation in terms of the backward coupling across a single cut. Bounds and numerical results for the 2D double-layer kernel suggest that truncation is close to optimal, and that the worst-case input field is a predominantly left-going grazing wave rather than backscatter of a right-going incident field. For a hard surface the inverse $L$-operator is given, up to a second-order correction, by four times the $L$-operator of the mirror-image surface, and several open questions are posed.

items.title: A Note on Binary Quadratic Systems and their relation to complexity theory
items.summary: Deciding whether a system of multivariate quadratic equations over $\mathbb F_2$ has a solution is a classical NP-complete problem, and remains so for square systems, with as many equations as variables. The hardness of this problem is one of the cornerstones of nowadays post-quantum cryptography. Let $\mathrm{MQ}_0(n)$ and $\mathrm{MQ}_1(n)$ denote the sets of square quadratic systems in $n$ variables having respectively no solutions and exactly one solution. $\cup_{n\geq 2} \mathrm{MQ}_0(n)$ is a coNP-complete language, while $\cup_{n\geq 2} \mathrm{MQ}_1(n)$ lies in DP. It is known that $\lim_{n\to \infty} |\mathrm{MQ}_1(n)|/|\mathrm{MQ}_0(n)|=1$. Here we prove the explicit finite-$n$ bounds \[ |\mathrm{MQ}_0(n)|<|\mathrm{MQ}_1(n)| \le \left(1+\frac{1}{2^n-1}\right)|\mathrm{MQ}_0(n)|, \] More generally, let $Q_d$ be the space of polynomial functions $(\mathbb{F}_2)^n\to\mathbb F_2$ of degree at most $d$, and let $α_k$ count square systems in $(Q_d)^n$ having exactly $k$ solutions. Then \[ α_0<α_1 \le \left(1+\frac{1}{2^n-1}\right)α_0\,, \qquad 2\le d\le n \,. \] The proof combines matroid and coding-theoretic methods. We interpret $(\mathbb{F}_2)^n$ as the ground set of the evaluation matroid of $Q_d$, express $α_0$ and $α_1$ through characteristic polynomials, and use a Whitney-type sign-reversing involution to show that the only terms that can push $α_1-α_0$ below $α_1/2^n$ come from the elements of a matroid port. These are identified with minimal-support words of the Reed--Muller code $\mathrm{RM}(n-d-1,n)=\mathrm{RM}(d,n)^\perp$; the required estimate then follows from the MacWilliams identity, the minimum-distance bound $2^{d+1}$, and the even-weight structure of the code.

items.title: On the Hermitian K-theory of Grassmannians
items.summary: We compute the $\mathbb{G}W$-spectrum (Karoubi--Grothendieck--Witt spectrum) of Grassmannians over divisorial schemes defined over fields of characteristic zero, and, as a corollary, determine their stabilized $\mathbb{L}$-theory spectrum. As part of our computation, we establish split fibration sequences in $\mathbb{K}$-theory, $\mathbb{G}W$-theory and $\mathbb{L}$-theory.

items.title: Polynomial identities and primitivity in double extension regular algebras of type (14641)
items.summary: We determine which members of the twenty-six families of double extension regular algebras of type $(14641)$ in the Zhang--Zhang classification satisfy a polynomial identity. Retaining the scalar twist parameter, we compute the PI degree for twenty-one of the twenty-two families with PI members and give three possibilities for the remaining family. We establish exact primitivity criteria for the nondegenerate members of eight families and show that sixteen families have no primitive members. The proofs use monomial data, normal subalgebras and crossed products of quantum tori. Twisting by a root of unity preserves the PI property, whereas finite order of the double-extension determinant is necessary but not sufficient for an algebra in the list to be PI.

items.title: Likelihood Geometry of Reflexive Polytopes
items.summary: We study the problem of maximum likelihood (ML) estimation for statistical models defined by reflexive polytopes. Our focus is on the maximum likelihood degree of these models as an algebraic measure of complexity of the corresponding optimization problem. We compute the ML degrees of all 4319 classes of three-dimensional reflexive polytopes, and observe some surprising behavior in terms of the presence of gaps between ML degrees and degrees of the associated toric varieties. We interpret these drops in the context of discriminants and prove formulas for the ML degree for families of reflexive polytopes, including the hypercube and its dual, the cross polytope, in arbitrary dimension. In particular, we determine a family of embeddings for the $d$-cube that implies ML degree one. Finally, we discuss generalized constructions of families of reflexive polytopes in terms of their ML degrees.

items.title: On some problems regarding a group-theoretical generalization of the Gauss formula
items.summary: In \cite{FT23}, we introduced the group-theoretical function $f(G) = \frac{1}{|G|}\sum_{H \le G} |\Aut(H)|$ for a finite group $G$ and posed three open problems concerning its values on noncyclic groups. In this note, we provide complete solutions to all three problems.

items.title: SL(n)-covariant symmetric tensor valuations on polytopes
items.summary: All $\operatorname{SL}(n)$-covariant symmetric tensor valuations on convex polytopes in $\mathbb R^n$ are completely classified without any continuity assumptions. It is shown that the only such valuation is the moment tensor.

items.title: Self-similar co-ascent processes and Palm calculus
items.summary: We study certain renormalised first passage bridges of self-similar processes, generalising the "Brownian co-ascent process" discussed by Panzo (Sém. Prob. L, 2019) and introduced by Rosenbaum and Yor (Sém. Prob. XLVI, 2014). We provide a characterisation of co-ascent processes via Palm measures, namely that the co-ascent of a self-similar process is the process under the Palm distribution associated with its record measure. We use this representation to derive a distributional identity for alpha-stable Lévy-subordinators with alpha in (0,1).

items.title: Propagation failure for bistable differential equations on periodic trees
items.summary: We study traveling fronts for bistable reaction-diffusion equations on periodic heterogeneous trees. We use comparison principles to estimate the pinning and propagation regions for both cubic and general bistabilities. Our analytical results and numerical simulations show that the interesting propagation reversal effects found in homogeneous trees become more pronounced in the heterogeneous setting, paving the way towards understanding more general graphs. As the diffusion strength increases, the waves end up moving in the same direction irrespective of the bistability. This direction is determined solely by the underlying structure of the heterogeneous tree. Our techniques also lead to sharper results for the homogeneous setting.

items.title: Product sets in sets of returns and positivity of symmetric ergodic averages
items.summary: We study sets of (measurable) returns in countable groups $G$, namely sets of the form $\{g\in G:μ(A\cap T_gA)>0\}$ arising from measure-preserving actions. Extending a result of Bergelson, we show that sets of returns in $G\times G$ contain subsets of the form $B\times B$, where $B$ is large with respect to suitable notions of largeness that remain meaningful even for non-amenable groups. As a consequence, if $G$ is amenable, then every sufficiently large subset $A\subseteq G\times G$ satisfies $B\times B\subseteq AA^{-1}$ for some large set $B\subseteq G$. We also investigate when sets of returns in $G$ contain product sets $BB$ with $B$ large. In contrast with the Cartesian-product phenomenon above, this problem is considerably subtler in non-abelian groups and is closely connected to `symmetric correlation functions', namely functions of the form $g\mapsto μ(T_g^{-1}A\cap T_gA)$. We use this connection to show that, for broad classes of amenable groups - including finitely generated nilpotent groups and certain solvable non-nilpotent groups, every sufficiently large set $A\subseteq G$ contains a large subset $B$ satisfying $BB\subseteq AA^{-1}$. Finally, we establish polynomial analogues of these results for finitely generated nilpotent groups, extending earlier work of Bergelson and Ruzsa.

items.title: Orbital Stability of Smooth Traveling Solitary Waves to the Fornberg-Whitham Equation
items.summary: The Fornberg-Whitham (FW) equation was introduced by Fornberg and Whitham [Fornberg and Whitham, Phil. Trans. R. Soc. Lond. A (1978)] as a nonlocal model for unidirectional shallow water waves capable of capturing wave steepening and breaking. Despite its similarities with integrable shallow-water equations, the FW equation is not completely integrable. Nevertheless, the FW equation is part of the family of peakon-type models as it supports peaked traveling wave solutions. In this paper, we consider smooth solitary wave solutions to the FW equation.
