We use a variational approach to show that some are orbitally stable.

items.title: Integrability and closed spacelike extremals of conformal arclength in the Einstein universe
items.summary: We study the conformal arclength functional for nondegenerate spacelike curves in the three-dimensional Einstein universe and classify its closed extremals up to conformal equivalence. We show that the extremals are projections of trajectories of a generically noncommutatively integrable Reeb flow. For extremals with nonconstant conformal invariants, closedness forces negative helicity and regular elliptic momentum. We prove that the restricted moment map over the corresponding invariant region defines a nontrivial principal $\mathbb T^3$-bundle, and construct explicit local trivializations that linearize the Reeb flow. This yields explicit parametrizations in terms of elliptic functions and integrals. We prove that the associated period map is a real-analytic diffeomorphism onto a bounded, convex planar domain whose rational points parametrize the conformal equivalence classes of closed extremals with nonconstant conformal invariants. We conclude with a study of the global geometry of closed extremals.

items.title: Ergodicity of the mapping class group action on components with small nonzero Euler number
items.summary: We study the action of the mapping class group on the $\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{R})$ character variety of a closed oriented surface of genus $g$. On the components considered here, the infimum of the translation lengths of essential simple closed curves is zero almost everywhere for every invariant positive Radon measure. For Goldman measure we show that almost every character sends some such curve to a non-hyperbolic element. By the criterion of Marche and Wolff, this proves Goldman's ergodicity conjecture for $g\ge 3$ and Euler numbers $e$ with $0<|e|\leq g-1$.

items.title: Ramsey-type results for Maker-Breaker games
items.summary: A graph $G$ is minimal Ramsey for a graph $H$ if every $2$-colouring of the edges of $G$ contains a monochromatic copy of $H$, but for every proper subgraph of $G$, there is a $2$-colouring that does not contain such a monochromatic copy. Characterizing minimal Ramsey graphs is a widely studied problem. Recent research in this field includes the characterization of the size of the set $\mathcal{M}_2(H)$ of all minimal Ramsey graphs for $H$, or finding the smallest minimum degree among all graphs in $\mathcal{M}_2(H)$. In this paper, we introduce a game theoretic analogue of the above concept by considering the Maker-Breaker $H$-game on a graph $G$. In this game, two players, Maker and Breaker, alternately claim unclaimed edges of $G$, and Maker wins if in the end of the game the graph spanned by Maker's edges contains a copy of $H$. Otherwise, Breaker wins the game. We call a graph $G$ winnable for $H$ if Maker has a winning strategy for the Maker-Breaker $H$-game on $G$, and we call it minimal winnable if additionally Breaker wins the $H$-game on every proper subgraph of $G$. Along the lines of minimal-Ramsey theory, we characterize all graphs $H$ for which there exist infinitely many minimal winnable graphs, and we prove tight bounds for the smallest minimum degree among all these minimal winnable graphs. Amongst others, we obtain precise results for trees, cycles, cliques, and complete bipartite graphs. In general, we find many similarities between the Ramsey setting and the Maker-Breaker setting, but we also show substantial differences.

items.title: List coloring degenerate graphs with requests
items.summary: We prove three results on the flexible list coloring of $d$-degenerate graphs. Following Dvořák, Norin and Postle [J. Graph Theory 2019], a graph $G$ is $(k,ε)$-flexible if for any assignment $L$ of lists of size $k$ to its vertices and any choice of requested colors by a set $\widehat V$ of the vertices from their respective lists, there is an $L$-coloring satisfying at least $ε|\widehat V|$ of the requests. The complete graph on $d+1$ vertices shows that if all $d$-degenerate graphs are $(k,ε)$-flexible for some list size $k$ and satisfaction ratio $ε$, then $k \geq d+1$ and $ε\leq\tfrac1{d+1}$. Our results concern values at or near these extremes. For list size $d+2$, we improve the satisfaction ratio from an inverse exponential to an inverse polynomial function of $d$. For satisfaction ratio $\tfrac1{d+1}$, we prove that it is achievable for list size $2d$ as well as $\left\lfloor(d+2)\left(2-\tfrac1e\right)\right\rfloor$ (which is less than $2d$ for $d\geq 9$).

items.title: Numerical algorithm for finding balanced metrics on polarized manifolds
items.summary: In \cite{D3}, Donaldson defines a dynamical system $T$ on the space of Fubini--Study metrics of a polarized manifold $(X,L)$, whose fixed points are the balanced metrics. In \cite{S}, Sano proves that the iterates of $T$ converge to a balanced metric, provided that a balanced metric exists and the automorphism group of $(X,L)$ is discrete modulo scalars. We remove the assumption on the automorphism group. Moreover, we show that the convergence is exponential with the optimal rate $ρ_*$ given by the linearization of $T$ at a balanced metric, which extends a result of Ioos and Polterovich (\cite{IP}) for discrete automorphism groups. We compute $ρ_*$ for $(\CP^n,\mathcal{O}(d))$ and $(\CP^1\times\CP^1,\mathcal{O}(d,d))$; for $\CP^1$ this confirms the rate obtained numerically by Sherman (\cite{Sh}).

items.title: Numerical algorithm for finding balanced metrics on vector bundles II: the non-simple case
items.summary: In \cite{D3}, Donaldson defines a dynamical system on the space of Fubini-Study metrics on a polarized compact Kähler manifold. Sano proved that if there exists a balanced metric for the polarization, then this dynamical system always converges to the balanced metric provided that the automorphism group is discrete (\cite{S}). In \cite{DKLR}, Douglas, et.\ al., conjecture that the same holds in the case of vector bundles. In \cite{Se}, we proved their conjecture under the assumption that the bundle is simple. In this note, we remove the simplicity assumption. The main tool is Thompson's metric on the space of Hermitian inner products on the space of holomorphic sections, with respect to which the generalized $T$-operator is non-expanding.

items.title: A Counterexample to Single-Control Null Controllability of Stochastic Heat Equations
items.summary: We disprove the conjecture that a single localized drift control suffices for null controllability of stochastic parabolic equations with bounded adapted coefficients. On a bounded interval with homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions, we construct a deterministic, nonnegative smooth noise coefficient supported at positive distance from the control interval. One fixed nonzero smooth initial state cannot be driven to zero almost surely at any positive time by any progressively measurable control with finite expected $L^2$ energy. The proof uses products of Brownian increments in the adjoint terminal data to keep the initial pairing bounded away from zero while the observation norm tends to zero. On the flat torus, the construction yields counterexamples in every Gevrey class of order $s>1$ whenever the complement of the control set contains an open ball. Thus Gevrey regularity above order one cannot replace analyticity as a general sufficient condition for null controllability.

items.title: Descartes' rule of signs for the topological degree
items.summary: We consider maps $F\colon\R^n_{>0}\to\R^n$ whose components are real polynomials, possibly with real exponents, with the same support of $N=n+k+1$ monomials, and we study the topological degree of $F$ on the positive orthant. In a previous paper we computed this topological degree in terms of signs of maximal minors, under a half-space condition which holds for generic exponents and coefficients. Here we use these formulas, together with their translation on the Gale dual side, to bound the topological degree. Our main result is a Descartes' rule of signs for the topological degree, which is as simple as the classical one: for two variables, the absolute value of the topological degree is at most half the number of cyclic sign changes, at the vertices of the Newton polygon, of the coefficients of any linear combination of the two equations, and similar statements hold in any dimension and on the Gale dual side. Our second result is a fewnomial bound: for generic exponents and coefficients, we get $|°F|<\frac12\min(M(n,N),M(k,N))$, where $M(d,N)$ is the maximal number of facets of a $d$-dimensional polytope with $N$ vertices, and this bound is sharp when $n=2$ or $k=2$. Our third result is a symmetry: using the H-duality of Bihan, Dickenstein and Forsgård, we show that the set of possible values of the topological degree is the same for the parameters $(n,k)$ and $(k,n)$.

items.title: Localizing spectra and pseudospectra of a class of unbounded operators on Hilbert space
items.summary: We use a localization technique to bound and approximate the spectrum and the pseudospectra of a certain class of possibly non-normal, generally unbounded but closed operators on $L^2(X)$, where $X$ is either a) a locally compact second-countable Hausdorff group $G$, not necessarily Abelian, with identity, a proper metric, and a left Haar measure or it is b) a uniformly discrete subset of $G$ with the counting measure. We treat the discrete and continuous cases b) and a) simultaneously. Our results yield computable subsets and supersets of the pseudospectra of $H$ that converge to the corresponding pseudospectrum in Attouch-Wets distance as the size parameter $L$ in our localization procedure goes to infinity. We illustrate our findings with unbounded band operators on $\ell^2(\mathbb Z)$ and with Schrödinger operators with $L^\infty_{\rm loc}$ potentials acting on $L^2(\mathbb R^d)$.

items.title: Critical exponents and near-critical limits for random matrix products
items.summary: We study the approach to the zero-Lyapunov-exponent transition for products of independent, identically distributed invertible matrices. The matrix laws are supported in a common compact subset of $GL(d,\mathbb{R})$ and converge in total variation to a strongly irreducible and proximal law with zero top Lyapunov exponent. We establish a near-critical renewal theorem for the occupation measure and a functional diffusion limit for the logarithmic cocycle as well as exact asymptotics and scaling limits for three observables describing the transient dynamics. The expected number of escapes from the unit ball and the expected number of visits to a fixed annulus diverge as the inverse absolute Lyapunov exponent, and both counts have exponential limits after normalization. The time spent on the side opposite to the asymptotic drift has critical exponent two and converges, after rescaling, to the positive occupation time of Brownian motion with negative drift.

items.title: CLT for Linear Spectral Statistics of sample covariances of superimposition of Separable Covariance Components
items.summary: Suppose $\{Z_r\}_{r=1}^K$ are $p\times n$ random matrices with entries having zero mean and unit variance and $p/n \to c \in (0,\infty)$. We construct the sample covariance matrix $S_n = \frac{1}{n}XX^*$ where $X =\sum_{r=1}^K X_r$, where $X_r = A_r^\frac{1}{2}Z_rB_r^\frac{1}{2}$, $K \in \mathbb{N}$ and $A_r,B_r$ are sequences of positive semi-definite matrices of dimensions $p\times p$ and $n\times n$, respectively that are are simultaneously digaonalizable within themselves. As an extension of our previous work related to the L.S.D. of such classes of matrices, we show that the linear spectral statistics arising from the spectra of $S_n$ have Gaussian limits under assumptions of fourth moment bounds on the entries of $\{Z_r\}_{r=1}^K$ and convergence of the joint spectral distribution of $\{A_r\}_{r=1}^K$ and $\{B_r\}_{r=1}^K$ to probability distributions over $\mathbb{R}_+^K$ with compact support.

items.title: Splitting of multiplicity spaces into symmetric and alternating parts
items.summary: For a finite dimensional semisimple Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$, the multiplicity $c_{λμ}^ν$ of an irreducible $V(ν),$ inside the tensor product $V(λ)\otimes V(μ),$ of two highest weight irreducible representations can be realised as the dimension of the Kostant--Parthasarathy--Ranga Rao--Varadarajan multiplicity space inside $V(λ)$, $V(μ)$ or $V(ν)$. A result of Panyushev and Yakimova shows how to split the multiplicity space for $c_{λλ}^ν$ inside $V(ν)$ into symmetric and alternating parts when $V(λ)$ is self-dual. For finite-dimensional semisimple or symmetric Kac--Moody, we extend this to Kostant--Kumar modules $K(λ,w,λ)=\mathfrak{Ug}(v_λ\otimes v_{wλ})$ when $w=w^{-1},$ and for all dominant weights $λ.$ We show that the multiplicities of an irreducible in the symmetric and alternating parts of $K(λ,w,λ)$ are given by the dimensions of the eigenspaces of the Tits lift $\widetilde w$ of $w$ on the multiplicity space corresponding to eigenvalues $\pm 1$. This recovers the result for the full tensor product by letting $w=w_0,$ the longest element of the Weyl group. In type A, we also discuss connections to a combinatorial interpretation due to Carré and Leclerc in terms of domino tableaux.

items.title: Generic bi-stochastic semigroups are flows
items.summary: We demonstrate genericity wrt. the weak polynomial topology of the space $\mathrm{Aut}(X, μ)$ of invertible measure-preserving transformations within the space of bi-stochastic operators over $L^{2}(X, μ)$ for standard probability spaces $(X, μ)$. This improves upon the approximation and residuality results established by Brown [4] and Kim [26] (cf. also [16]). We make crucial use of a reformulation of the Birkhoff--von Neumann theorem [2, 43] due to Kim for bi-stochastic operators over infinite dimensional Hilbert spaces. This enables the construction of stochastic processes, via which dilations and thereby $\mathrm{PW}$-approximations may be obtained. In a similar fashion, we demonstrate the weak-genericity of weakly-continuous measure-preserving flows on $(X, μ)$ within the space of $\mathcal{C}_{0}$-semigroups of bi-stochastic operators on $L^{2}(X, μ)$. To achieve this, we make use of random measures (viz. Poisson point processes) and build on our discrete-time result. This complements recent advances in ergodic theory due to Furlong on the genericity of measure-preserving flows in the space of measure-preserving semi-flows.

items.title: Pettis integrability of $L^1$-functions in locally convex spaces
items.summary: In this article, for a Hausdorff locally convex space $E$, we investigate conditions under which every Lusin-measurable $L^1$-function $γ:[0,1]\to E$ is Pettis integrable. We show that this property on $E$ is local and equivalent to $E$ being absolutely summable and satisfying the metric convex compactness property. Via examples, we show that these two properties are independent. Moreover, we establish sufficient conditions, for a Lusin-measurable weakly integrable function with values in the topological dual $E'$, to be Gelfand integrable.

items.title: The pentagonal tensor and the fourth obstruction to formality
items.summary: Let \(A\) be a connected graded commutative differential graded algebra over \(\mathbb Q\) whose cohomology is a finite-dimensional Poincaré duality algebra of formal dimension \(N\ge2\). Assuming that its Bianchi-Massey tensor vanishes, we prove that the normalized pentagonal tensor of Nagy and Nordström, in [preprint (2021), arXiv:2105.13660], vanishes if and only if the fourth Harrison obstruction vanishes after eliminating the third operation. This gives a fourth-order counterpart to the third-order comparison of Fiorenza and Lê, in [Ann. Sc. Norm. Super. Pisa Cl. Sci. (5), published online 7 March 2025], and answers the vanishing question in Lê's proposed comparison, in [preprint (2026), arXiv:2603.01219], under the hypothesis that the Bianchi-Massey tensor vanishes. The result applies to closed, connected, oriented manifolds with no upper dimension bound. We also extend Zhou's sphere-bundle formality criterion in [Algebr. Geom. Topol. 25 (2025), pp. 2297--2315] to two-stage oriented sphere bundles with positive odd fibre dimensions over a closed, connected, oriented, rationally formal base, provided that the second Euler class is pulled back from the original base. Their total spaces are rationally formal precisely when the Bianchi-Massey and normalized pentagonal tensors vanish. Our method develops the model-based strategy in Zhou's proof within a commutative bar-cobar framework, providing a starting point for constructing higher tensors and comparing them with higher-order formality obstructions.

items.title: Variational Principles and Machine Learning: a Numerical Analysis and PDE perspective
items.summary: Variational principles have played a fundamental role in the development of modern mathematics, physics, and scientific computing. From the principles of least action in mechanics to the calculus of variations and the variational formulation of partial differential equations, they have provided a powerful framework for understanding complex problems and designing reliable numerical methods. In recent years, Machine Learning has introduced a new computational paradigm, in which highly expressive nonlinear function spaces and large-scale minimisation problems play a central role. In these notes, we explore the connection between these two frameworks. We develop a variational and numerical-analysis perspective on Machine Learning algorithms, focusing in particular on their formulation as nonlinear minimisation problems. We investigate how classical concepts such as stability, consistency, approximability, and compactness acquire new interpretations in this setting, and how the variational structure of the underlying continuous problem can govern the behaviour of neural-network approximations. This perspective provides a mathematical framework for understanding existing ML algorithms while also suggesting new approaches to their design. In particular, alternative and strongly coercive variational principles can lead to more stable, reliable, and potentially more efficient computational methods.

items.title: Measurable equidecomposability and the Banach--Ruziewicz problem over locally compact non-Archimedean valued fields
items.summary: We prove a measurable analogue of the Banach--Tarski paradox over locally compact non-Archimedean valued fields. Let $\mathbb K$ be the completion of a number field at a non-Archimedean place (e.g., $\mathbb K=\mathbb Q_p$) and $n\ge 2$. Then any two bounded Haar measurable subsets of $\mathbb K^n$ with nonempty interior and equal Haar measure can be cut into finitely many Haar measurable pieces and rearranged into each other by elements of a certain countable group $Γ$ of affine isometries. We also show that the Haar measure is, up to a constant factor, the unique nonzero finitely additive $Γ$-invariant measure on the bounded Haar measurable subsets of $\mathbb K^n$, which solves a $p$-adic version of the Banach--Ruziewicz problem. Both results follow from the fact that the action of $Γ$ on $\mathbb K^n$ is expanding, a property closely related to the spectral gap. For $n=1$ and arbitrary characteristic, we obtain analogous results when the residue field is not prime, using a countable group of isometries that are not necessarily affine.

items.title: The enigma of locally Toeplitz matrices. I. Discrete Schrödinger operators with complex potential
items.summary: Freezing the coefficients of a banded locally Toeplitz matrix gives a family of Toeplitz eigenvalue measures. Their average can fill a region of the complex plane even when the eigenvalues of the original matrices appear to follow curves. We conjecture that, when the above average has a sufficiently regular planar density, the limiting eigenvalue measure is its mother body. We prove it for a class of finite Dirichlet discrete Schrödinger operators with complex potential $V$ and a common real coefficient $α>0$ on the two adjacent diagonals. When $(\Im V)'>0$ and $V$ admits a suitable holomorphic extension, the limiting measure is supported on finitely many analytic arcs. Its logarithmic potential falls below that of the averaged measure by twice the least of four explicit actions. We obtain these actions from a four-term asymptotic expansion of the Dirichlet determinant. When $\Im V$ is not monotone, an exact transfer recursion gives a conditional extension. For a circular potential arc we verify the geometric switching condition, leaving non-resonance as the remaining hypothesis.

items.title: The $k$-disjoint paths problem for group-labelled graphs
items.summary: A $Γ$-labelled graph is an oriented graph with edge labels in a group $Γ$. Fix a finite abelian group $Γ$ and a positive integer $k$. We give a polynomial-time algorithm that finds $k$ vertex-disjoint paths joining prescribed pairs with a prescribed gain on each path, or determines that none exist. The result previously appeared only in the author's 2009 PhD thesis. This proof uses a reduction to unbreakable graphs and recent structure theorems for graphs drawn on a surface, and was found with the help of AI.

items.title: A Joint Functional Central Limit Theorem for the $L^p$-Norm Profile of Random Littlewood Polynomials
items.summary: For a random Littlewood polynomial $q_n(z)=\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}\varepsilon_jz^j$ with independent Rademacher coefficients, let $S_n(θ)=|q_n(e^{iθ})|^2/n$ be its normalized angular intensity. Its positive moments $T_n^{(p)}=\|q_n\|_p^p/n^{p/2}$ form the moment profile of the intensity distribution under normalized arc measure on the unit circle. We prove a joint functional central limit theorem for this profile. For $p$ in a compact interval $K\subset(0,\infty)$ and logarithmic time $n=\lfloor Ne^t\rfloor$, $t\in[-T,T]$, the piecewise linear interpolations of $\sqrt n(T_n^{(p)}-Γ(1+p/2))$ converge to a Gaussian field $G(p,t)$ in $C(K\times[-T,T])$. The corresponding step processes converge in $D([-T,T];C(K))$ with the Skorokhod $J_1$-topology. The limit has the representation $G(p,t)=\sum_{a=2}^{\infty}c_a(p)G^{(a)}(t)$, where $c_a(p)$ are the ordinary Laguerre coefficients of $x^{p/2}$, with $L_a(0)=1$. The independent centered stationary Gaussian modes have covariance $\mathrm{Cov}(G^{(a)}(s),G^{(a)}(t))=2V_a e^{-(a-1/2)|t-s|}$, where $V_a$ is the squared $L^2$-norm of the density of the sum of $a$ independent uniform random variables on $[0,1]$. We also obtain the functional limit theorem for $\|q_n\|_p/\sqrt n$ and identify its joint covariance. At $p=4$, we recover the known scalar autocorrelation fluctuation law and identify its dependence across nested lengths. Finite-mode convergence follows from the multivariate functional de Jong theorem after model-specific variance, influence, and fourth-moment calculations. Maximal estimates control the infinite Laguerre tail and its exponent derivative uniformly over nested lengths.

items.title: Converse comparison of $g$-expectations and uniqueness of generators of BSDEs: a novel approach and some sharp results
items.summary: This paper investigates inverse problems for backward stochastic differential equations (BSDEs), with a particular focus on the converse comparison theorem and the uniqueness of generators solely through the initial values of the corresponding solutions. To this end, we develop a forward-SDE representation approach that combines a contradiction argument with a representation of generators in terms of solutions to associated forward stochastic differential equations (SDEs). As one of the main consequences, we prove that an ordering between two $g$-expectations necessarily implies the pointwise comparability of their generators, without requiring any additional structural assumptions beyond the standard Lipschitz condition. This removes the continuity, $y$-independence, and deterministic assumptions required in previous works, thereby yielding a complete solution to the converse comparison problem for $g$-expectations under the standard Lipschitz framework and, at the same time, establishing a general uniqueness theorem for generators of BSDEs.

items.title: Rigidity and flexibility results for groups with a common cocompact envelope
items.summary: A locally compact group $G$ is a cocompact envelope of a group $Γ$ if $G$ contains a copy of $Γ$ as a discrete and cocompact subgroup. We study the problem that takes two finitely generated groups $Γ,Λ$ having a common cocompact envelope, and asks what properties must be shared between $Γ$ and $Λ$. We first consider the setting where the common cocompact envelope is totally disconnected. In that situation we show that if $Γ$ admits a finitely generated nilpotent normal subgroup $A$, then virtually $Λ$ admits a normal subgroup $B$ such that $A$ and $B$ are virtually isomorphic. We establish both rigidity and flexibility results when $Γ$ belongs to the class of solvable groups of finite rank. On the rigidity perspective, we show that if $Γ$ is solvable of finite rank, and the locally finite radical of $Λ$ is finite, then $Λ$ must be virtually solvable of finite rank. On the flexibility perspective, we exhibit groups $Γ,Λ$ with a common cocompact envelope such that $Γ$ is solvable of finite rank, while $Λ$ is not virtually solvable. In particular the class of solvable groups of finite rank is not QI-rigid. We also exhibit flexibility behaviours among finitely presented groups, and more generally among groups with type $F_n$ for arbitrary $n \geq 1$.

items.title: Topological degree of sparse polynomial maps
items.summary: We consider maps $F\colon\R^n_{>0}\to\R^n$ whose components are real polynomials, possibly with real exponents, with the same support $\A$, and we study the topological degree of $F$. We prove a real analogue of the Bernstein--Kushnirenko--Khovanskii theorem, which says that the number of solutions in the complex torus is the normalized volume of the Newton polytope when there is no solution at infinity. Our main assumption is a half-space condition on the columns of the coefficient matrix indexed by the faces of the Newton polytope. It is a positive analogue of the absence of solutions at infinity, and it is satisfied for generic exponents and coefficients. Under this condition, we show that the topological degree only depends on the oriented matroids of the exponent and coefficient matrices restricted to the vertices of the Newton polytope. We give two closed formulas for it: a sum over the facets of the Newton polytope, and a Viro formula, which is a signed count of the positively decorated simplices of a regular triangulation of $\A$. As a consequence, we get sign conditions for the existence of positive solutions, as well as parity results for their number.

items.title: Automorphism groups of Severi--Brauer varieties of odd prime degree over $\mathbb{Q}$
items.summary: We prove that the only non-trivial finite subgroup of automorphism group of non-trivial Severi--Brauer variety of odd prime degree $p$ over the field of rational numbers is $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}.$

items.title: Cooperative colorings of cycles and uniform cycle factors
items.summary: A cooperative coloring of graphs on a common vertex set is a choice of one independent set in each graph such that their union covers the vertex set. We give a combinatorial proof that three cycles on a common vertex set always have a cooperative coloring. We also prove that, for every $\ell\geq4$ with $\ell\equiv1\pmod3$, there are three graphs on a common vertex set, each a disjoint union of cycles of length $\ell$, with no cooperative coloring. Together with known bounds, this determines, for every $\ell\geq3$, the least number $m$ such that every $m$ graphs on a common vertex set, each a disjoint union of cycles of length $\ell$, have a cooperative coloring. For $\ell\geq3$, this number is four when $\ell\equiv1\pmod3$ and three otherwise. These results answer two questions of Aharoni, Holzman, Howard, and Sprüssel.

items.title: On the connected zero forcing polynomial of finite trees
items.summary: Given a graph $Γ$ with vertex set $V(Γ)$ and a set of colored vertices S, the zero forcing rule is an iterative graph coloring process which states that a colored vertex with exactly one uncolored neighbor forces that neighbor to become colored. If repeated application of this rule eventually colors every vertex of $Γ$, the set $S$ is called a \emph{zero forcing set}. Now, if the induced subgraph $Γ\vert_S$ is connected, then $S$ is called a \textit{connected zero forcing set}. The minimum cardinality of such a set is the \emph{connected zero forcing number} $Z_C(Γ)$. A \emph{connected zero forcing polynomial} of a finite graph $Γ$ is a monic polynomial $Z_C^Γ(x) \;=\; \sum_{k} a_k x^k$, where $a_k$ counts the number of connected zero forcing sets of $Γ$ of size $k$, which we denote by $Z_C(Γ,k)$. In this paper, we find the connected zero forcing polynomial of any finite tree $T$, and show that they are log-concave. We then establish sharp lower bounds for each coefficient of the connected zero forcing polynomial, over all trees on $n$ vertices with $p$ many pendant vertices. We also identify a family of trees, which we call uniform trees, and we prove that for any tree on $n$ vertices and $p$ many pendant vertices, there exists a uniform tree on $n$ vertices and $p$ many pendant vertices, whose connected zero forcing polynomial bounds as an upper bound, the connected zero forcing polynomial of the tree coefficient wise. Again for $2\leq p\leq 4$, we establish a sharp upper bound for each coefficient of the connected zero forcing polynomial, over all trees on $n$ vertices with $p$ many pendant vertices.

items.title: The hitting time index: bounds, a sharp threshold, the proof of a conjecture and the disproof of another conjecture
items.summary: We prove some new upper and lower bounds for the hitting time index ($HT$ index) of an $n$-vertex graph, showing along the way that the largest order of the index is $n^5$ and the smallest is $n^3$. More specifically, we prove the conjecture that the smallest value of the index is $\frac{n(n-1)^2}{2}$, which is attained by the complete graph. We also find a sharp threshold for the minimal degree $δ$ so that the $HT$ index goes from an $n^4$ order to an $n^3$ order if the threshold is surpassed. We disprove the conjecture that the largest value of the index is attained by the $n$-path, and look at the lollipop graphs, some of which attain the $n^5$ order, and seem to be the natural candidates among which the largest value of the index should be attained.

items.title: Separation formulas for non-normalized generalized cluster algebras
items.summary: We study a class of not necessarily normalized generalized cluster patterns which are uniquely determined by the initial seed and mutations. For such generalized cluster patterns, we provide the separation formulas for cluster variables and coefficients.

items.title: A Short Proof of the Goldman--Parker Conjecture
items.summary: Goldman and Parker conjectured that the three order-two complex side reflections of an ideal triangle with Cartan angular invariant $A$ define a discrete and faithful representation of $\mathbb Z/2 \ast \mathbb Z/2 \ast \mathbb Z/2$ in $PU(2,1)$ whenever $\tan^2 A\le 125/3$. Schwartz first proved the conjecture using rigorous computer-assisted estimates and later gave an analytic proof based on three loxodromic $\mathbb R$-spheres. We give a substantially shorter proof of this conjecture using a simpler geometric construction. For parameters just below the critical value, we use the Cygan bisector of the two fixed points of the triple product of the reflections. This wall and one of its cusp translates bound a strip from which we construct a trapping region. At the critical value $\tan^2 A=125/3$, the two fixed points merge, and the same construction applies to the limiting wall.

items.title: A note on mean field games of controls with state constraints: existence of mild solutions
items.summary: We show the existence of mild solutions for a first-order mean field game of controls under the state constraint that trajectories be confined in a closed and bounded set in euclidean space. This extends the results of Cannarsa and Capuani to the case of a mean field game of controls. Our controls are velocities and we find that the existence of an equilibrium is complicated by the requirement that they should have enough regularity. We solve this by imposing a small Lipschitz constant on the dependence of the Lagrangian on the joint measure of states and controls.

items.title: Extremals and Normalized Solutions for a Critical Weighted Choquard Equation
items.summary: We study normalized solutions to the weighted Choquard equation \[ \left\{ \begin{aligned} -\operatorname{div}(|x|^{-2a}\nabla u) &=λ|x|^{-2a}u+β|x|^{-bq}|u|^{q-2}u\\ &\quad+|x|^{-bp} \left( \int_{\mathbb R^N} \frac{|u(y)|^p}{|x-y|^μ|y|^{bp}}\,dy \right) |u|^{p-2}u &&\text{in }\mathbb R^N,\\ \int_{\mathbb R^N}|x|^{-2a}u^2\,dx&=ρ^2, \end{aligned} \right. \] where $N\ge3$, $a<(N-2)/2$, $a<b<a+1$, $2<q<2^\sharp$, $0<μ<N$, $p=(2N-μ)/(N-2d)$ is the upper Stein--Weiss critical exponent, $d=1-b+a$, $2^\sharp=2N/(N-2-2a+2b)$, $ρ>0$ is prescribed, $β>0$, and $λ\in\mathbb R$ is an unknown Lagrange multiplier. Assuming $p>2$, we establish existence and multiplicity of normalized solutions in different mass regimes, including negative-energy ground states for small $β$ and positive-energy second solutions under suitable assumptions, as well as ground states in the mass-critical and mass-supercritical cases under explicit conditions

items.title: Sharp decay and regularity thresholds for Minkowski stability in spherical symmetry
items.summary: We establish sharp decay and regularity thresholds for Minkowski stability in the spherically symmetric Einstein--scalar field system. For small smooth characteristic data measured in weighted derivative seminorms, we prove global stability at borderline decay and half-derivative regularity of the initial data. The resulting developments remain uniformly close to Minkowski spacetime and are future causally geodesically complete. Both thresholds are sharp: below either the decay or regularity threshold, we construct arbitrarily small smooth, initially untrapped data whose developments contain trapped spheres.

items.title: Irreducible trinomials over the binary field: an elliptic-curve criterion and explicit families
items.summary: We study irreducible trinomials over $\mathbb{F}_2$. Using an elliptic curve and reciprocity laws, we prove that, for $k \ge 2$, $X^{(4^k+2)/3}+X+1$ is irreducible if and only if $4^k+3$ is prime and $2$ is a primitive root modulo that prime. By power substitution and linearization, we also assemble explicit infinite families of irreducible trinomials $X^m+X^n+1$ in fourteen distinct reduced exponent classes.

items.title: Global well-posedness for the focusing Gross-Pitaevskii equation in the one-dimensional Zhidkov space
items.summary: We show global well-posedness for the focusing Gross-Pitaevskii equation in one spatial dimension, with initial data in the Zhidkov space, with no smallness condition. For the usual nonlinear Schrödinger equation with decaying initial data, a mass-energy argument is used to preclude finite-time blow-up. Here both mass and total energy are infinite, but we put together a renormalized version of that bound by using the net mass transfer and the kinetic energy, which we show are a priori bounded. Global well-posedness on the energy space and on $1+H^1$ follows. We also treat a variant of the equation with a smooth real density response to show how this construction can be generalized to different nonlinearities.

items.title: The Kao-Lai-Osting Conjecture for the Second Laplace Eigenvalue on Riemannian Two-Tori
items.summary: We prove the $k=2$ case of the Kao-Lai-Osting conjecture for the area-normalized Laplace spectrum of Riemannian two-tori: $\sup_g λ_2(T^2,g)\,\mathrm{Area}(T^2,g) = 8π^2/\sqrt{3} + 8π$, where the supremum is taken over smooth Riemannian metrics. No smooth metric attains this value. It is approached by a sequence in the equilateral conformal class developing a round spherical bubble, and the equilateral class is the only conformal class whose conformal supremum equals the global one. The upper bound follows from spherical folding and a sharp truncated conformal-area inequality for fundamental embeddings into $S^5$. Normal-curvature and normal-chord estimates yield high-cap area control, with exact elementary estimates on nested high-centre strips. The proof is partly computer-assisted. Rational polynomial inequalities handle the low-weight cap range and the entire residual high-cap region, the latter through exact Bernstein certificates on rational boxes, which are also checked independently in ball arithmetic. The residual product inequality is established by rigorous upper quadratures, with two independent reproducible certificates, in ball and in interval arithmetic, and exact domain-coverage checks.

items.title: Degree-respecting labellings with ordered neighbour sums
items.summary: In an exhaustive enumeration of hydrocarbons with only single bonds, carbon skeletons are generated as adjacency matrices and pruned by two rules: a vertex of larger degree receives a smaller label, and among vertices of equal degree, a vertex whose adjacency row is the larger binary integer receives a smaller label. The pruning is sound only if every skeleton admits a labelling obeying both rules. We prove that such a labelling exists for every finite simple graph, connected or not and with no bound on the degrees, and that the same holds when the weights $2^i$ of the labels $i$ are replaced by any strictly increasing real weights. The proof takes, among the labellings that order vertices by non-increasing degree, one minimising the sum over edges of the products of the endpoint weights.

items.title: List packing for graphs with small arboricity
items.summary: We prove that every graph $G$ whose edge set is the union of $r$ forests has list packing number at most $2^r$. This means that for all $k\ge 2^r$ and every list-assignment $L$ with lists of size $k$, the graph $G$ admits $k$ disjoint proper $L$-colourings. While for large $r$ this bound is far from optimal, for $r\in\{1,2\}$ it is sharp. As a direct corollary of the case $r=2$, we obtain that every triangle-free planar graph has list packing number at most $4$, thus improving upon a result of Dvořák, Masařík, Musílek and Pangrác and providing the optimal answer to a question of Dvořák, Postle and Norin on (weighted) $ε$-flexibility of such graphs. As a corollary of the case $r=3$, we obtain a short alternative proof that every $K_5$-minor-free (and hence every planar) graph has list-packing number at most $8$, matching the state of the art. All results above also hold for the stronger notion of correspondence packing.

items.title: Mean field game value multifunction: dynamic programming principle
items.summary: We study mean field games (MFGs) on the torus with non-degenerate diffusion, in a regime (no monotonicity) where multiple solutions exist for the same data. In this setting the value of a representative player is not a function of the initial time and distribution, and the classical master equation loses its meaning. We describe the dependence of the value on the initial data by a multivalued mapping, the value multifunction, assigning to each initial time and distribution the set of value functions of all solutions of the MFG starting from that data. Our main result gives a sufficient condition for a closed multifunction to be a value multifunction, namely, it must satisfy a dynamic programming principle formulated on proper time subintervals, expressed as invariance of its graph under the forward operators generated by equilibria of the game. This replaces the global requirement that each value be produced by a solution of the forward-backward system on the whole time interval by a local, time-consistent condition together with closedness, which carries the terminal condition. The result is the second-order analogue of the viability approach previously developed for first-order mean field games. We reformulate solutions of the mean field game in terms of relaxed equilibria, show that the closure of a value multifunction is again a value multifunction, and prove that the forward operators compose as a semigroup. We also present an explicit example in which a single terminal cost produces at least two solutions for every initial time in an interval, while solutions are unique for initial times sufficiently close to the horizon.

items.title: Prophet Inequalities for Mixtures of I.I.D. Random Variables
items.summary: A latent index $J\in\{1,\ldots,k\}$ is drawn from a prior $π$. Conditional on $J=j$, a gambler observes random variables $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ drawn independently from a non-negative component distribution $F_j$. The gambler knows $n$, the prior $π$, and the component distributions $F_1,\ldots,F_k$, but not $J$, observes the values sequentially, and selects at most one value at the time it is revealed. We show that the largest $α$ such that the gambler can guarantee to select a value of $α\cdot\mathbb{E}[\max_iX_i]$ in expectation, for all distributions where this expectation is finite, is \[ α=\frac1e+\frac{1}{k^{2/3+o(1)}}. \] The lower bound is achieved by the better of two variants of the standard secretary rule. The upper bound uses a finely tuned instance of the common-scale model, which scales a sequence of independent random variables by a single latent variable.

items.title: Policy Iteration Is Not Polynomial for Deterministic Markov Decision Processes: The Price of Algorithmic Anarchy
items.summary: We establish exponential iteration lower bounds in the number of states for Howard's policy iteration on deterministic discounted and average-reward Markov decision processes (MDPs), with a constant number of actions per state. This rules out polynomial-time complexity of Howard's policy iteration in both settings. We further prove that a Dantzig counterpart of Howard's policy iteration runs in strongly polynomial time on deterministic average-reward MDPs. Together with the known strongly polynomial bound for Dantzig's rule on deterministic discounted MDPs, these results establish an exponential separation between the two algorithms in both settings. This separation between Howard's decentralized and simultaneous selfish improvements and Dantzig's coordinated selection of a single action with the largest improvement across all states reveals a "price" of algorithmic anarchy.

items.title: A nonfinitely based additively idempotent semiring with finitely based matrix semirings
items.summary: We establish that the matrix semiring $\mathbf{M}_n(SR_6)$ over the six-element nonfinitely based additively idempotent semiring $SR_6$ is finitely based for every $n \geq 2$. This provides the first known example of an additively idempotent semiring $S$ that is nonfinitely based, while the matrix semirings $\mathbf{M}_n(S)$ are finitely based. Moreover, we show that the interval $[\mathsf{V}(SR_6), \mathsf{V}(\mathbf{M}_2(SR_6))]$ in the lattice of additively idempotent semiring varieties has the cardinality of the continuum.

items.title: Development of a GPU-accelerated numerical simulation model for liver infection in realistic domains
items.summary: Viral hepatitis reduces the functionality of the liver and constitutes a major global health concern because it oftentimes evolves to chronic inflammation leading to long term liver damage. Mathematical models on a mesoscopic scale abstract from only partly known cell-scale processes while providing an in-silico tool for understanding tissue-scale development of the disease. In this work, we investigate the interactions between virus and immune cells in a realistic three-dimensional liver geometries by using a reaction-diffusion model that reproduces infection courses with cure and with chronic developments. A GPU-based finite-difference implementation, released as an open-source Python library, achieves speedups greater than x30 for realistic mesh sizes, making three-dimensional simulations on realistic geometries computationally tractable. This provides a basis for future in-silico studies of treatment strategies, such as testing antiviral or immunomodulatory therapies, and for patient-specific simulations based on individual liver geometries, paving the way towards personalized healthcare.

items.title: Integrable nearest neighbor interaction Hamiltonians and the rigidity of the Toda Lattice
items.summary: We consider mechanical Hamiltonian systems, where the potentials describe a nearest-neighbor interaction law. In this setting, a non trivial example of an integrable system is the celebrated Toda lattice. We study deformations of this potential (for three particles), and show that some classes of analytic deformations of the potential break its integrability, without assuming anything about the form of the integrals. This result is reminiscent of local rigidity of ellipses in billiards. The proof relies on the fact that high energy orbits for the Toda lattice approximate billiard orbits in some polytopes.

items.title: A square analogue of the diamond order and a unified approach to the plus order
items.summary: We introduce the square order $\le^\square$ on group invertible matrices, defined by $A^3=ABA$ and $A\le^s B$, where $\le^s$ is the space pre-order. It is the group inverse analogue of the diamond order: $A\le^\square B$ if and only if $A^\#\le^- B^\#$. Using its block representation, we characterize the reverse order law $(AB)^\#=B^\#A^\#$ for $A\le^\square B$. In contrast to the Moore--Penrose case, the conditions $A\le^- B$ and $(B-A)^\#=B^\#-A^\#$ do not characterize the sharp order; instead, they lead to new partial orders between the sharp and square orders. We also develop a framework where the plus order replaces the minus order in Mitra's unified theory. For a map $\mathcal G$ assigning to each matrix $A$ a subset of its inner inverses, we define $A\le^{\mathcal G}_{+}B$ if $A\le^s B$ and $A=PBQ$ for some pair $(P,Q)=(AA^-,A^-A)$, $A^-\in\mathcal G(A)$, whereas Mitra's relation requires $A=PB=BQ$, and $A\preceq^{\mathcal G}_{+}B$ if $A\le^s B$ and $A^-\le^-B^-$ for some reflexive $A^-\in\mathcal G(A)$ and $B^-\in\mathcal G(B)$. When $\mathcal G(A)$ consists of a single reflexive inverse, we characterize the transitivity of $\le^{\mathcal G}_{+}$ in terms of $\preceq^{\mathcal G}_{+}$, and in general we give a sufficient condition for both to be partial orders. For maps defined by the equations of the Moore--Penrose, group, core and dual core inverses, both relations coincide and only nine arise: the plus, diamond and square orders, two new orders based on core inverses, and four further relations. In Mitra's theory, they yield exactly the minus, star, sharp, core and dual core orders and the one-sided star and sharp orders.

items.title: Deterministic integer factorization from abundance decisions
items.summary: We prove that deciding whether a positive integer is abundant is equivalent to complete integer factorization under deterministic polynomial-time Turing reductions. In particular, abundance can be decided in deterministic polynomial time if and only if integers can be factored in deterministic polynomial time. Our reduction uses carefully chosen coprime multipliers to recover exact divisor sums from abundance queries, and then extracts the complete prime factorization of an integer $n$ deterministically from the divisor sums of $O(\log n)$ consecutive powers of $n$. Altogether, factoring $n$ requires $O((\log n)^4)$ adaptive abundance queries, each at an integer of $O((\log n)^6)$ binary digits.

items.title: On the Fueter--Sce--Qian theorem for partial-slice monogenic functions
items.summary: The notion of partial-slice monogenic functions has recently been introduced to provide a unified framework encompassing both monogenic and slice monogenic functions over Clifford algebras. In this new setting, we establish some fractional Laplacian identities for the Cauchy kernels and their derivatives in the sense of tempered distributions. These identities allow us to prove a termwise Fueter--Sce--Qian theorem for partial-slice monogenic functions represented by convergent Laurent series consisting only of principal parts.

items.title: Deformations of Locally Conformal Parallel Spin(7) Instantons
items.summary: We study the infinitesimal deformation theory of $Spin(7)$-instantons on compact locally conformal parallel (LCP) $Spin(7)$ manifolds, that is, $Spin(7)$ manifolds whose fundamental 4-form satisfies $dΦ=θ\wedgeΦ$ with a closed, non-exact Lee form $θ$. We show that the gauge-fixed linearized instanton equations are equivalent to a kernel problem for a twisted Levi-Civita Dirac operator $\mathcal{D}^-_A-\mathcal{A}_θ\colonΓ(\mathcal{S}^-\otimes\mathfrak{g}_P)\toΓ(\mathcal{S}^+\otimes\mathfrak{g}_P)$, compute the zeroth-order term $\mathcal{A}_θ$ explicitly, and show that its pointwise squared operator norm equals $\frac{49}{64}|θ|^2$. Combined with the Lichnerowicz--Weitzenböck formula and Ivanov's scalar curvature identity, this yields a sufficient condition for rigidity, which we show can never be satisfied by flat connections. Indeed, the trivial connection is never rigid: its deformation space contains $H^1(M;\mathbb{R})\otimes\mathfrak{g}$. Our main result concerns the product LCP manifolds $N\times S^1$, where $N$ is a compact nearly parallel $G_2$ manifold: for the pull-back of a $G_2$-instanton $B$ on $N$ we prove $\mathcal{H}^1_{Spin(7)}(\mathrm{pr}^*B)\cong\mathcal{H}^0_{G_2}(B)\oplus\mathcal{H}^1_{G_2}(B)$. This reduces the deformation theory of such instantons to the nearly parallel $G_2$ case, shows that this containment is an equality for the trivial connection, and produces non-flat examples on the Hopf manifold $S^7\times S^1$ and on other products with homogeneous nearly parallel $G_2$ manifolds.

items.title: Neur2BiLO: Neural Bilevel Optimization
items.summary: Bilevel optimization deals with nested problems in which a leader takes the first decision to minimize their objective function while accounting for a follower's best-response reaction. Constrained bilevel problems with integer variables are particularly notorious for their hardness. While exact solvers have been proposed for mixed-integer linear bilevel optimization, they tend to scale poorly with problem size and are hard to generalize to the non-linear case. On the other hand, problem-specific algorithms (exact and heuristic) are limited in scope. Under a data-driven setting in which similar instances of a bilevel problem are solved routinely, our proposed framework, Neur2BiLO, embeds a neural network approximation of the leader's or follower's value function, trained via supervised regression, into an easy-to-solve mixed-integer program. Neur2BiLO serves as a heuristic that produces high-quality solutions extremely fast for four applications with linear and non-linear objectives and pure and mixed-integer variables.

items.title: $L^p$ Integrability and Spectral Complexity of Manifolds with Higher Codimension
items.summary: We investigate the relationship between the $L^p$ integrability of functions and the curvature geometry of their Fourier support. We prove that if $M\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ is a $C^n$ manifold of dimension $d$ and $n>2d$, then every $u\in L^p(\mathbb{R}^n)$ with $\operatorname{supp}\widehat u\subseteq M$ vanishes whenever \[ 2\le p\le\frac{6n-4}{3d-1}. \] This strictly improves the classical threshold $2n/d$ throughout the range $n>2d$. More generally, we obtain a family of dimension-dependent improvements in higher codimension. As a consequence, we obtain a strict quantitative improvement in the necessary conditions for Fourier restriction when $n>2d$, resolving a conjecture of Mockenhaupt \cite{Mockenhaupt96}. This further establishes the nonexistence of quadratic manifolds satisfying the Christ--Mockenhaupt condition when $n>2d$, answering the question of \cite{CLMP}. For quadratic manifolds, we obtain spectral synthesis bounds from joint sublevel estimates for the eigenvalues of the normal Hessian pencil. In codimension two, we determine the exact critical exponent from the ranks and eigenvalue vanishing orders, including nonexistence at the critical endpoint. We also obtain integrability bounds for manifolds with constant relative nullity, extending Guo's hypersurface results \cite{Guo93} to higher codimension. Finally, we use the Fourier ratio as a measure of the geometric complexity of individual strata of the characteristic set to establish $L^p$ uniqueness criteria for homogeneous constant-coefficient PDEs.

items.title: Polynomial-degree-robust saturation on triangular meshes
items.summary: We prove a polynomial-degree-robust ($p$-robust) saturation property for conforming finite element approximations of the Poisson equation on shape-regular triangular meshes. Previously, a $p$-robust saturation estimate for the spectral method on a square was proved in [C. Canuto et al., A saturation property for the spectral-Galerkin approximation of a Dirichlet problem in a square, ESAIM Math. Model. Numer. Anal., 53 (2019), pp. 987--1003]. For every fixed $λ>1$, increasing the polynomial degree from $p$ to any $q\geq\lceilλp\rceil+3$ reduces the energy error by a factor $α_λ\in(0,1)$ independent of $p$ and the mesh size, up to a data oscillation term.

items.title: Regularity Criteria for Ind-Sheaves
items.summary: In this paper, we prove the Kashiwara-Schapira regularity conjecture [Conjecture 6.4, Masaki Kashiwara and Pierre Schapira, Microlocal study of ind-sheaves I: micro-support and regularity, 2003] in arbitrary dimension. For this purpose, we show that under suitable finiteness and isotropic micro-support conditions, ind-sheaves which are regular on the zero section come from $\mathbb{R}$-constructible sheaves. Furthermore, we characterize the essential image of constructible sheaves under the natural embedding functor, and relate them to regular holonomic $\mathcal{D}$-modules via the regular Riemann-Hilbert correspondence. Moreover, we present a non-characteristic deformation lemma and a microlocal Morse lemma for regular ind-sheaves as an application of the main theorem.

items.title: Certified Return-Word Induction for a Perturbed Hofstadter Recursion: Global well-definedness, local frequencies and nonautomaticity
items.summary: We study the parity-perturbed Hofstadter recursion $Q(1)=Q(2)=1$, $Q(n)=Q(n-Q(n-1))+Q(n-Q(n-2))+(-1)^n$. We give a computer-assisted proof of global well-definedness using 13 return words, 92 synchronized states and 122 two-source rules. An induction on the rank words identifies the four ordered physical source projections at every level. The marked word construction and a finite lag certificate then identify its binary output with the step word $s_j=(Q(j+1)-Q(j-1))/2$ of the recursion. We determine the frequency of $001100$ in prefixes of $s$ as a function of the position within each pair of epochs. After rescaling the prefix length by $4^m/3$, the frequency converges uniformly to an explicit profile. Its minimum $1/96$ and maximum $1/48$ are the exact lower and upper limiting frequencies, and every value between them is a subsequential limit. The longest alternating factor among the first $N$ steps has length $2\log_2 N+O(1)$. It follows from Cobham's gap theorem that neither the step word nor $Q\bmod 4$ is automatic in any integer base $k\ge 2$.

items.title: Weak-strong stability and uniqueness of measure-valued solutions to (nonlocal) pressureless Euler-type systems
items.summary: We consider the pressureless Euler equation possibly coupled with non-local forces like the Poisson and alignment interactions. We overcome the lack of strict convexity in the relative entropy inequality that arises from the lack of pressure. The key to this result is the appropriate framework of the solution scheme utilizing the generalized Young measure which yields extra structural properties for the oscillation and concentration parts of the measure-valued solution. We overcome the problem of density mismatch via two complementary techniques. The first takes advantage of a Figalli--Kang-type transport inequality. The second involves establishing a generation lemma for the generalized Young measure which simultaneously establishes $L^2$-based control in flat metric between the measure-valued density and the density generating sequence.

items.title: Hadwigerś Covering Conjecture in Three Dimensions
items.summary: Let $K \subset \R^3$ be an arbitrary convex body, that is, a compact convex subset of $\R^3$ with nonempty interior. We prove unconditionally that $K$ can be covered by eight smaller positive homothetic copies of itself: there exist a scalar $λ\in (0, 1)$ and translation vectors $v_1, \dots, v_8 \in \R^3$ such that \[ K \subseteq \bigcup_{i=1}^{8} (λK + v_i). \] This resolves Hadwiger's covering conjecture in three dimensions. The proof works in Boltyanski's equivalent boundary illumination formulation and is completely self-contained. Parallelepipeds are covered directly by eight translates of $\frac{2}{3} K$. For any convex body $K$ that is not a parallelepiped, we place its centrally symmetric halved difference body $S = \frac{1}{2}(K - K)$ in John's position ($B^3 \subseteq S$) and show that the spherical average of its support function satisfies $8 \int_{S^2} h_S \, d\sigmatilde < 12$, with equality only for orthogonal cubes. Using outer polyhedral approximations together with Cauchy's planar perimeter formula, the full spherical measure of directions not parallel to any boundary segment of $K$, and lower semicontinuity of curve variation, we find a unit vector $w_* \in S^2$ whose shadow boundary $\Shad{K}{w_*}$ on $K$ itself is a continuous closed curve of $S$-length strictly less than $12$. Splitting $\Shad{K}{w_*}$ into six contiguous arcs of $S$-length strictly less than $2$ and applying Helly's theorem in $\R^3$ illuminates each arc with one direction, while $\pm w_*$ illuminate the remainder of $\partial K$. The proof was discovered using an experimental harness on top of Gemini~4 Carbon and formally verified in Lean~4.

items.title: A Characterization of Douglas Weights
items.summary: A weight $ω$ on the unit disc is a \emph{Douglas weight} if the $ω$-energy of the Poisson extension of every Lipschitz function $f$ on the unit circle equals $\iint|f(ζ)-f(λ)|^2\,d\J_ω$ for some positive symmetric measure $\J_ω$ off the diagonal. For radial weights, we show that this holds if and only if \[ j_ω(θ) = \int_0^1 \frac{ω(r)}{r}\, \partial_θ^2 P(r^2,θ)\,dr \geq 0, \qquad 0<θ\leqπ, \] where $P(x,θ)$ denotes the Poisson kernel. We also obtain a complete characterization of the Douglas weights among arbitrary weights. The class of Douglas weights strictly contains the nonnegative superharmonic weights, and we give examples that are neither superharmonic nor subharmonic.

items.title: The arithmetic of critical values II: critical elliptic curves
items.summary: In this second chapter of the \textit{Arithmetic of critical values} series (ACV), we study certain double covers $E_f\to\mathbb{P}^1$ whose branch locus coincides with that of a quartic polynomial $f$. We give a direct proof of the fact, already shown non-constructively in ACV I, that the elliptic curves $E_f$ admit a $3$-isogeny. Our methods lead us to examine the Galois closure of $f:\mathbb{P}^1\to\mathbb{P}^1$, whose rich geometry yields a congruence between $E_f$ and a second elliptic curve $E'_f$. We study their arithmetic and show that they are linked by a Selmer companionship for infinitely many $f\in\mathbb{Z}[X]$, allowing us to exhibit elements in certain Tate-Shafarevich groups which are visible in an abelian surface. We also give some dynamical and Diophantine applications of our constructions, as well as new examples of Jacobians isogenous to a power of an elliptic curve.

items.title: Ramification divisors and twisted Nambu brackets of Keller maps
items.summary: For a polynomial map $φ\colon\A^n\to\A^n$ we study the Yau twist of the Jacobian Nambu bracket by $φ^*$. The Hamiltonian fields of pulled back functions span the image of the adjugate of $dφ$, so the twist detects the ramification divisor of $φ$. For a Keller map $F$ the twist is removable exactly when $F$ is an automorphism; otherwise $F$ is not proper, and every projective extension of $F$ has a non-zero effective ramification divisor supported on the boundary, whose image is the non-properness set. These results apply to every counterexample to the Jacobian conjecture and to families of Keller maps. For the explicit three-dimensional counterexample we show that $\A^3$ is the variety of binary cubic forms of a special shape with a marked simple root, and that $F$ forgets the root. This gives the degree, the fibres, the non-properness set, the monodromy and the structure of the twisted ternary algebra. Three examples modelled on weighted scrolls illustrate equivariance, degeneration to an automorphism, and an $A_1$ singularity of the fibre.

items.title: A Coarse-Geometric Interpretation of Holt's One-End Theorem
items.summary: Can a group be colored red and blue, with both color classes infinite, so that each right translation changes the color of only finitely many elements? For the group of finite subsets of the natural numbers, one can color a nonempty set by the parity of its largest element (and the empty set red). Holt proved that no such coloring exists in an uncountable locally finite group. For the finitary coarse structure, right almost invariant subsets are exactly the coarsely clopen sets; modulo finite changes, their characteristic functions give all the projections in the Higson corona algebra. We give a detailed, self-contained account of Holt's coset argument in Cornulier's formulation, without using group cohomology. The argument shows why the space of coarse ends is a singleton and the full Higson corona is connected. We then give a proof of Protasov's stronger conclusion for any uncountable abelian group---in particular, an uncountable direct sum of groups of order two---showing that the full Higson corona is a singleton.

items.title: A zero-one law for one-shot system identification
items.summary: Can a model be identified from one experiment? We study analytic systems that are linearly parameterized by a combination of prescribed dictionary terms, such as partial differential operators and dynamical systems. For a single input-response pair, recovery is possible exactly when the evaluated dictionary terms are linearly independent. We prove a sharp zero-one law: either no input uniquely determines the coefficients, or almost every random input sampled from a nondegenerate Gaussian measure does. This dichotomy reduces one-shot system identification to a question about degenerate inputs and provides an a posteriori certificate in the noiseless setting. Numerical examples recover dynamical systems, nonlinear partial differential equations, and structured matrix families from single trajectory data, while also detecting when an extra probe is necessary.

items.title: Curvature inequalities and rigidity for constant mean curvature and spacetime constant mean curvature surfaces
items.summary: We establish curvature inequalities and rigidity results for constant mean curvature (CMC) surfaces in Riemannian manifolds and spacetime constant mean curvature (STCMC) surfaces in Lorentzian manifolds. In three-dimensional Riemannian manifolds with nonnegative scalar curvature, we show that the Christodoulou-Yau inequality $H^2\leq 16π/|Σ|$ ($H$ denoting mean curvature and $|Σ|$ area) for stable CMC spheres also holds for CMC surfaces of arbitrary topology under a new stability condition controlling only the constant mode of the second variation of area. Under an extrinsic curvature sign condition, equality forces the enclosed region to be Euclidean without additional intrinsic assumptions. We extend these results to higher dimensions and to the hyperbolic and spherical settings. In the Lorentzian setting, we develop a variational stability theory for STCMC surfaces based on the second variation of area in the mean curvature vector direction. We introduce two independent stability notions: variational stability, which recovers classical volume-preserving CMC stability for surfaces in totally geodesic spacelike hypersurfaces, and constant-mode stability. Under the dominant energy condition, either yields the sharp inequality $|\vec H|^2\leq 16π/|Σ|$. In the equality case, under suitable geometric assumptions, the maximal globally hyperbolic development of the enclosed spacelike region is a Minkowski causal diamond. These results imply nonnegativity and rigidity of the Hawking quasi-local energy for stable STCMC surfaces. Finally, we analyze known spacelike and null STCMC foliations, showing that asymptotic leaves are stable under positive mass conditions, whereas the local matter density and trace-free extrinsic curvature govern the instability of local foliations.

items.title: An algorithm to compute upper bounds of dimensions for Siegel Modular Forms of Prime Level and Arbitrary Nebentypus
items.summary: We describe an algorithmic method to determine the image of restriction maps for Siegel modular forms with \textit{arbitrary} characters and arbitrary weight. A program has been implemented in the mathematical software \texttt{Java} to compute the Fourier expansion of the image of these restriction maps for Siegel modular forms of genus two. This approach allows us to compute an upper bound for the space of Siegel modular forms with {\it non-trivial} character (which has not been previously known) and arbitrary weights (including low weight $k \leq 4$).

items.title: The capillary $L_{p}$ dual Christoffel-Minkowski-type problem for $p\geq q$ with $1\leq k\leq n$
items.summary:
We study the following fully nonlinear $k$-Hessian equation on a spherical cap $\mathcal{C}_θ$ for $1\leq k\leq n$ and $0<θ<π/2$: $$ \left\{  egin{aligned} σ_k(
abla^2h+hσ) &=fh^{p-1} igl(h^2+|
abla h|^2 igr)^{ rac{k+1-q}{2}} &&	ext{in }\mathcal{C}_θ,\ 
abla_μh&=\cotθ\,h &&	ext{on }\partial\mathcal{C}_θ. \end{aligned} ight. $$ Under suitable convexity and boundary assumptions on $f$, we establish the existence of positive smooth strictly convex solutions for $p\geq q$, together with uniqueness when $p>q$ and $p\geq 1$. In the critical case $p=q>1$, scaling invariance prevents uniform $C^0$ estimates without normalization. We overcome this difficulty using a logarithmic gradient estimate and a normalized approximation with uniqueness up to dilation.

items.title: Normal abelian subgroups of order 5^6 in finite 5-groups
items.summary: A finite 5-group containing an abelian subgroup of order 5^6 has a normal abelian subgroup of that order. If the given subgroup is elementary abelian, the normal subgroup can be chosen elementary abelian. This resolves n=6, the last open case of both parts of Problem~21.51 of the Kourovka Notebook for p=5. Together with earlier results, it follows that 1\le n\le 6 is the exact range in which each assertion holds for every finite 5-group at subgroup order 5^n. In a minimal counterexample, five conjugate abelian subgroups generate a group of class at most three. In class two we construct invariant isotropic subgroups for the commutator pairing. In class three the Jacobi identity produces a nonzero plane cubic over the field of five elements. The five conjugate subgroups give five distinct singular points spanning the plane, which forces the cubic to vanish.

items.title: Norm groups of orders and the algebraic unknotting number
items.summary: We use number-theoretic tools to find an explicit and effective obstruction for a knot to have algebraic unknotting number equal to $1$. As an example, we show that the connected sum of $T(2,5)$ (the cinquefoil) and $-T(2,3)$ (the negative trefoil) has algebraic unknotting number $1$, even though $T(2,5)$ has algebraic unknotting number $2$.

items.title: The confined discrete DLSS equation: gradient flow structure and long-time asymptotics
items.summary: We propose and analyse a structure-preserving discretization of the fourth-order DLSS equation in dynamically rescaled variables leading to a linear confinement on the one-dimensional real line. The scheme is obtained as a discrete analogue of the Carrillo--Toscani splitting. It allows for a new interpretation of the DLSS equation as gradient flow of the relative entropy with respect to a combined diffusive and transport metric, extending the structure of the discretization introduced in our earlier work with Giuseppe Savaré for the unconfined equation. We prove global existence of positive solutions and, as the main analytical result, exponential decay of the relative entropy towards the discrete Gaussian equilibrium. The decay rate is obtained via a discrete modified logarithmic Sobolev inequality. The resulting rate is consistent with the continuum rate and converges to it from below in the vanishing mesh-size limit. Numerical results illustrate and confirm our findings.

items.title: On the applicability of the maximality principle in optimal stopping: an example involving a diffusion and its running maximum
items.summary: The maximality principle has proved to be a valuable tool for identifying the optimal stopping boundaries in optimal stopping problems involving one-dimensional time-homogeneous diffusions and their running maximum processes. The principle characterises the optimal stopping boundary as the maximal solution to a first-order nonlinear ODE that remains strictly below the diagonal in $\mathbb{R}^2$ or a "zero-level curve". In this paper, we construct a suitably tailored optimal stopping problem to which the maximality principle is not applicable.

items.title: On the First Derivative Bounds for Rational Bézier Curves
items.summary: We derive a new upper bound for the first derivative of a rational Bézier curve of degree $n$. The estimate applies to arbitrary degrees and provides a framework for studying the linear bound conjectured by Li et al., whose coefficient is the maximal adjacent weight ratio $Ω$. Within this framework, the conjectured bounds for $n=5$ and $n=6$ are established as special cases, completing the verification for all $n\le6$. The endpoint estimates follow from the classical derivative formulas. For interior parameters, the analysis reduces to a variance-like optimization problem over a compact box of adjacent weight ratios. A block argument reduces the maximization to vertices and one-dimensional faces, leading to a finite family of polynomial inequalities. We further prove that sufficiently fine subdivision yields subcurves satisfying the conjectured estimate with their own weights, control points and local parameters. After parameter rescaling, these local estimates provide a bound for the derivative of the original curve. Numerical examples illustrate the new bound and the subdivision-based estimates and compare them with an existing method.

items.title: Generic non-convergence of low-temperature Ising Glauber dynamics on $\mathbb Z^2$
items.summary: We study how typical convergence is, in the topological sense of Baire category, for the heat-bath Glauber dynamics of the nearest-neighbour, zero-field Ising model on $\mathbb Z^2$ started from translation-invariant initial laws. At sufficiently low positive temperature, we show that the initial laws whose evolution has both the plus and the minus phase as weak subsequential limits form a dense $G_δ$ subset of the space of translation-invariant laws with the weak topology. Consequently, the initial laws for which the dynamics converges in distribution form a meagre set, which gives a partial answer to an open problem posed by Liggett. In particular, a large initial magnetisation does not force convergence to the plus phase, even for spatially ergodic initial laws. The proof combines equilibrium and mixing estimates of Gheissari and Sly with a periodic grid of plus spins of vanishing density and Baire's theorem, and it applies to all reversible monotone Glauber dynamics for the Ising model.

items.title: Time-consistency of cash-subadditive risk measures: The infimal cocycle property
items.summary: We characterize the time-consistency of convex, cash-subadditive dynamic risk measures in terms of their minimal penalty. The dual variables are conditional sub-probability densities, which factorize across an intermediate date in many ways, according to how the discount is allocated to the two periods. We introduce an infimal cocycle property, in which the penalty is the infimum over all such factorizations, and show that it is equivalent to time-consistency, with the infimum attained. This holds on $L^\infty$ under continuity from below, and on $L^p$, $p<\infty$, without continuity assumptions. In the cash-additive case it reduces to the classical cocycle property. For risk measures induced by BSDEs, it represents the dynamic programming principle of a stochastic control problem whose value is the penalty.

items.title: Veronese Classification of Constant-Curvature Minimal Two-Spheres in Complex Hyperquadrics
items.summary: We prove that every linearly full, irreducible conformal minimal immersion of constant Gaussian curvature and finite isotropy order from the two-sphere into a complex hyperquadric comes from a member of a Veronese sequence. The result holds at every finite isotropy order, without an unramifiedness or additional Frenet-norm polynomiality assumption. Both the associated projective harmonic sequence and the target harmonic sequence are totally unramified as consequences. If the replacement depth is \(\ell\) and the holomorphic seed spans \(\mathbb{CP}^m\), the curvature is \(K=2/((2\ell+1)m-2\ell^2)\) in the Grassmannian normalization. Real Gram data characterize the admissible embeddings and give an algebraic converse. The proof uses holomorphic Pfaffian norm identities, degree estimates that retain all ramification divisors, and a valuation argument that identifies the retained lines with seed Frenet lines.

items.title: Simultaneous Inversion of Drift and Potential in the Fractional Magnetic Schrödinger Equation
items.summary: We study the Calderón problem for the fractional magnetic Schrödinger equation with drift in the bivariate additive framework. When the magnetic potential $A$ is known and fixed, we prove that the drift $b$ and the scalar potential $q$ can be simultaneously and uniquely determined from exterior Dirichlet-to-Neumann measurements. When $A$ is unknown, we prove that the triple $(A,b,q)$ can only be recovered up to a natural gauge equivalence class, and that the drift $b$ is a gauge invariant, hence uniquely determined. The proofs rely on the Alessandrini identity, Runge approximation, and the unique continuation property for fractional magnetic operators. Furthermore, we have developed a numerical reconstruction framework that combines finite difference discretization, radial basis function surrogate modeling, and smoothed TV regularization. One-dimensional and two-dimensional numerical examples have verified the effectiveness of the proposed method and supported the theoretical uniqueness result.

items.title: Tensor ideals of oligomorphic permutation categories
items.summary: We classify tensor ideals for oligomorphic permutation categories $Perm(G,μ)$. To this end we define an equivalence relation on the class of transitive smooth $G$-sets. We show that there is a bijection between the tensor ideals of $Perm(G,μ)$ and the downward-closed subsets of the poset of equivalence classes. As a corollary we obtain that there is a bijection between tensor ideals and thick tensor ideals. We determine the poset in many cases (mostly in characteristic $0$): the infinite symmetric group, wreath products, products of oligomorphic groups, equivariantizations, finite groups in positive characteristic and the classical groups $GL, O, Sp, U$ over a finite field.

items.title: Independence of Thurston eigenvalues and Lyapunov exponents for quadratic rational maps
items.summary: We study post-critically finite quadratic rational maps $f: \mathbb{P}^1\to\mathbb{P}^1$ where the two critical points lie in the same cycle. The Thurston eigenvalues of $f$ are those of the derivative of the Thurston pullback map $σ_f$ at its fixed point. Addressing questions of Buff--Epstein--Koch, we construct a sequence of real, bitransitive centres in the critical orbit relation curve $C_2$ which degenerates in moduli space, and whose Lyapunov exponents tend to infinity whilst the Thurston eigenvalues satisfy $\frac{1}{10}< |λ|<1$. We also show the Thurston eigenvalues across all bitransitive centres in $C_2$ have a spectral gap on compact subsets of the curve.

items.title: Derivative Estimation from Coarse, Irregular, Noisy Samples: An MLE-Spline Approach
items.summary: We address numerical differentiation under coarse, non-uniform sampling and Gaussian noise. A maximum-likelihood estimator with $L_2$-norm constraint on a higher-order derivative is obtained, yielding spline-based solution. We introduce a non-standard parameterization of quadratic splines and develop recursive online algorithms. Two formulations---quadratic and zero-order---offer tradeoff between smoothness and computational speed. Simulations demonstrate superior performance over high-gain observers and super-twisting differentiators under coarse sampling and high noise, benefiting systems where higher sampling rates are impractical.

items.title: A note on characterization of S4 x C2^n
items.summary: For every non-negative integer n, we characterize S4 x C2^n by its poset of isomorphic classes of subgroups. This provides an infinite family of counterexamples to the conjectures posed by Tarnauceanu in [8] and [9].

items.title: Rigidity of Constant-Curvature Minimal Two-Spheres in Complex Hyperquadrics at Isotropy Order $n-6$
items.summary: We classify linearly full, irreducible, totally unramified conformal minimal two-spheres of constant Gaussian curvature in the real Grassmannian $G(2,n;\mathbb R)$, or equivalently in the complex hyperquadric $Q_{n-2}$, whose finite isotropy order is $n-6$, where $n\geq7$. We remove the additional polynomiality assumption on a Frenet norm in the earlier classification of Li and Jiao. An exterior-product norm identity reduces the problem to the multiplicity of the irreducible polynomial $1+zw$; a further divisibility argument handles the boundary dimension $n=7$, including isotropy order one. The dimension $n$ is necessarily odd, and the immersion is congruent, after a conformal reparametrization, to the second member of a Veronese sequence with its prescribed real structure. Its curvature is $2/(5n-13)$ in the Grassmannian normalization. An explicit model in $Q_5$ illustrates the boundary case and its harmonic sequence.

items.title: On generalized linear periods for inner forms of GLn
items.summary: Let $\mathrm{D}$ be a central division algebra of index $e$ over a non-Archimedean local field $\mathrm{F}$ of characteristic zero.
